one_line_idea: Restoration models should output a hallucination map, and cross-seed variance of generative restorers already provides one that flags fabricated regions.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Generative restoration outputs mix recovered evidence and prior-invented content with no indication of which is which.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-pixel dispersion across sampling seeds is a usable hallucination indicator: regions with high cross-seed variance are dominated by prior invention, and exposing this map materially changes user trust decisions.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Cross-seed variance maps will overlap substantially with regions where outputs deviate from ground truth on synthetic tasks, and will flag most human-identified hallucinations on real tasks. Falsified if: cross-seed variance maps flag <= 50% of human-identified hallucinations on the real-task validation set.
why_important: A standard hallucination-disclosure output would make generative restoration auditable, which matters for forensic, journalistic, and archival uses.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sample diversity is studied as a quality, but standardizing seed-variance as a hallucination disclosure channel with validation against ground truth may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate multiple seeds per input on synthetic pairs, compute variance maps, and measure overlap with actual error maps; then validate on real images with human hallucination annotation.
main_risk: Consistently wrong regions (confident hallucination across seeds) evade the variance signal, so the map has a known blind spot.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Restoration outputs are presented as single images, with uncertainty communication considered out of scope.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Where evidence constrains the posterior, seeds agree; where the prior dominates, seeds disagree; this is exactly the recoverable-versus-invented distinction users need, available at zero training cost.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Sample a public diffusion restorer several times on one degraded face or text image, compute the pixel variance map, and check visually whether high-variance regions coincide with implausible or fabricated detail.

judge_A_meta.tension_note: vs H-037: cross-seed variance is a usable hallucination map vs diversity is misallocated (varies irrelevant texture, collapses where ambiguity matters). Adjudicate by experiment, not dedup.

one_line_idea: Sample diversity in stochastic restoration is misallocated: seeds vary irrelevant texture while collapsing on semantically ambiguous content where diversity actually matters.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Stochastic restorers advertise multiple plausible outputs as a feature representing posterior uncertainty.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-seed variation concentrates in perceptually irrelevant micro-texture while semantically ambiguous regions (which face, which character) collapse to a single mode, so the advertised diversity does not represent the true posterior where it counts.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Decomposing cross-seed variance into semantic and textural components will show textural variance dominating by a large factor, and constructed inputs with genuinely multimodal semantic posteriors will yield single-mode outputs across seeds. Falsified if: in the stated two-way decomposition of cross-seed variance into semantic and textural components, the textural component accounts for <= 50% (does not exceed the semantic component).
why_important: Users interpreting sample spread as uncertainty will be misled precisely on high-stakes ambiguous content.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Diversity is reported as pixel spread; auditing whether diversity aligns with true posterior multimodality may be unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct degraded inputs consistent with several distinct semantic ground truths, sample restorers many times, and measure how often distinct semantic modes appear versus texture-only variation.
main_risk: Constructing verifiably multimodal inputs requires care; accidental evidence leakage would make mode collapse look correct.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Sample spread is presented and consumed as a proxy for posterior uncertainty.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Mode-seeking training dynamics and guidance both suppress rare modes; texture has many near-equivalent optima while semantics has few distinct ones, so variance flows to texture by construction.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Downsample an image containing a digit until ambiguous between two digits, sample a public restorer many times, and count whether both digits ever appear; persistent single-digit output demonstrates semantic collapse.

judge_A_meta.tension_note: vs H-030 (see above); also vs J-056/J-057 which assert dispersion tracks true ambiguity in dense diffusion samplers.

one_line_idea: Fixed default guidance scales in diffusion restoration are wrong for most images, and per-image guidance calibration from consistency residuals recovers substantial quality for free.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion restorers ship with a single guidance or conditioning-strength default that trades evidence adherence against prior-driven sharpness, applied uniformly across inputs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The optimal guidance scale varies widely per image with degradation severity and content, and a cheap automatic calibrator that picks the scale by minimizing re-degradation residual plus a realism proxy beats any fixed scale on average.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Oracle per-image scale selection will beat the best fixed scale by a clear margin, and the automatic calibrator will capture most of that oracle gap. Falsified if: the automatic residual-based guidance calibrator captures <= 50% of the oracle per-image scale-selection gain over the best fixed scale.
why_important: It is an inference-time improvement requiring no retraining, applicable to all deployed diffusion restorers.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Guidance sensitivity is known, but closed-loop per-image guidance calibration for restoration via forward-model residuals may be unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sweep guidance per image on a benchmark to establish oracle gains, then implement residual-based automatic selection and measure the captured fraction of the oracle gap.
main_risk: The realism proxy in the selection objective could import metric-gaming biases into the calibrator.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] A well-tuned global guidance default is assumed near-optimal across inputs.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Evidence strength varies by orders of magnitude across degradation severities; a single scale must over-trust the prior on mild inputs or under-trust it on severe ones.
fastest_falsification_experiment: For a handful of images at different severities, sweep the guidance scale of one public model and record the visually best setting per image; large per-image disagreement in best settings proves the fixed default is suboptimal.

one_line_idea: Generative restorers are unstable inverse maps: imperceptible input perturbations flip hallucinated semantic content, undermining forensic use.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Adversarial sensitivity is documented for classifiers, while restoration models are increasingly used to enhance evidentiary imagery.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Tiny, imperceptible perturbations of a degraded input can deterministically switch semantically meaningful restored content (different characters, different facial features), demonstrating that restored semantics are functions of noise-level input details no honest analyst would consider informative.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Gradient-based search will find perturbations far below visibility thresholds that change restored text or identity attributes in targeted directions, succeeding on most tested inputs. Falsified if: targeted gradient-based perturbation search at perturbation norms below the study's visibility threshold changes restored text or identity attributes in the targeted direction on <= 50% of the tested inputs.
why_important: If restored semantics can be steered by invisible input changes, restoration outputs must be inadmissible as evidence, and products need stability disclosures.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Adversarial attacks on SR exist for quality degradation; targeted semantic steering of hallucinated content in modern generative restorers may be unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define semantic targets (specific characters or attributes), run targeted perturbation search on degraded inputs against public restorers, and measure success rates and perturbation norms.
main_risk: Stochastic samplers complicate attack evaluation, requiring expectation-over-seeds attack objectives.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Restoration outputs are informally trusted as deterministic functions of visible input content.
why_it_might_be_wrong: In evidence-poor regions the posterior is nearly flat, so infinitesimal input changes can move the sampled mode; instability is a structural property of prior-dominated inversion, not a bug.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Add tiny random perturbations (not even adversarial) to an ambiguous degraded text crop and re-restore; observing semantic flips across perturbations already demonstrates instability.

judge_A_meta.anomaly_note: imperceptible input perturbations deterministically flip hallucinated semantic content — restored semantics are functions of noise-level details (forensic significance)

one_line_idea: Generative restorers can inject memorized training images into outputs on ambiguous inputs, and restoration needs a memorization-probe protocol like generation has.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Training-data memorization and regurgitation are documented in unconditional and text-conditional generative models, while restoration models trained on the same data families lack analogous audits.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When observation evidence is weak, restoration models sometimes complete inputs with near-copies of specific training images (faces, artworks, scenes), constituting a privacy and copyright hazard that current evaluation never surfaces.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Nearest-neighbor retrieval between restored outputs and the training corpus will uncover above-chance rates of high-similarity matches in evidence-poor regions, increasing with degradation severity and prior capacity. Falsified if: the rate of high-similarity training-corpus matches for restored outputs in evidence-poor regions is at or below the matched-control (chance) rate.
why_important: Restoration is marketed as recovering the user's own content; injecting other people's memorized content is a qualitatively different and legally significant behavior.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Memorization audits exist for generation; a restoration-specific probe protocol conditioned on degradation severity may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Restore heavily degraded inputs with models whose training corpora are accessible, retrieve nearest training neighbors of outputs in feature space, and compare match rates against matched controls.
main_risk: Distinguishing memorized injection from generic prior knowledge requires careful similarity thresholds and controls.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Restoration models are assumed to synthesize generic detail rather than reproduce specific training instances.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Restoration training rewards exact reconstruction of training targets; under weak evidence the cheapest loss reduction is recalling training content, which is the definition of memorization pressure.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feed near-uninformative inputs (extreme downsampling) to a restorer trained on a known accessible corpus and retrieve nearest training neighbors of the outputs; conspicuous matches would appear in a small-scale probe.

one_line_idea: The field needs a formal restoration-versus-reimagination boundary based on information recoverable from the observation, and most perceptual SR crosses it without disclosure.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Restoration and generation are marketed as distinct, yet modern perceptual SR outputs contain large amounts of content not determined by the input observation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] An operational criterion comparing observation-derived information against prior-injected information per region can classify outputs into restoration and reimagination regimes, and applying it will show that popular perceptual SR operates mostly in the reimagination regime at high magnification factors.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Estimated prior-injected information share will exceed observation-derived share for most output content at large scale factors, with a sharp regime transition as magnification grows. Falsified if: at the largest tested scale factor, the estimated prior-injected information share exceeds the observation-derived share on <= 50% of the evaluated output content.
why_important: A disclosed, measurable boundary would let products and papers label outputs honestly and let regulation reference an operational standard.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] The distinction is discussed philosophically, but an operational per-region information accounting for restoration may not have been formalized.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define estimators for observation-derived versus prior-injected information (via forward-model consistency and conditional entropy proxies), validate on synthetic cases with known ground truth, and apply to popular models across scale factors.
main_risk: Information estimates on images are approximation-heavy, and the boundary could be contested as estimator-dependent.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Perceptual SR is presented and consumed as restoration, with generation framing reserved for text-to-image tools.
why_it_might_be_wrong: At high magnification the observation contains a small fraction of the output's information content by simple counting arguments, so the output is necessarily mostly prior; the only question is making this measurable.
fastest_falsification_experiment: At increasing scale factors, measure how much output content survives when the conditioning is replaced by a different image with the same coarse structure; high survival indicates prior domination and locates the regime boundary cheaply.

one_line_idea: Vision-language-guided restoration converts caption errors into confident pixel hallucinations, a compounding error mode absent from caption-free restorers.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Some restoration pipelines condition on automatically generated captions or vision-language descriptions of the degraded input to inject semantic guidance.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When the captioner misreads degraded content, the restoration inherits and amplifies the error, rendering the wrong semantics with high visual confidence, so caption guidance is net-harmful on exactly the ambiguous inputs it was meant to help.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On inputs where the captioner errs, caption-guided restoration will produce more semantically wrong content than the same model without caption guidance, and total error will be dominated by caption-induced cases at high degradation severity. Falsified if: at the highest tested degradation severity, caption-induced cases account for <= 50% of the caption-guided restorer's total semantic errors.
why_important: Language-guided restoration is an appealing trend; identifying its compounding failure mode determines when it should be disabled.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Caption guidance is proposed for quality; an error-propagation analysis from captioner to pixels may not have been published.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate a caption-guided restorer with correct, automatically generated, and deliberately corrupted captions on synthetic degradations, and attribute semantic errors to caption versus image pathways.
main_risk: Guidance strength varies across implementations, so the effect size may be pipeline-specific.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Semantic guidance from language models is assumed to add robustness under severe degradation.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The captioner sees the same degraded evidence the restorer does, so it adds no new information, only a hard semantic commitment made before pixel evidence is weighed.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feed a caption-guided restorer a degraded image with a subtly wrong caption and observe whether the output follows the caption against the visual evidence; caption-following on a few examples demonstrates the pathway.

one_line_idea: Universal all-in-one restoration models suffer negative transfer on hard cases, losing to per-task specialists at matched capacity despite average-metric parity.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Foundation-style restoration models advertise a single network handling denoising, deblurring, SR, and inpainting, reporting strong averaged benchmark results.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Multi-task restoration training induces negative transfer concentrated in the hardest quantiles of each task, so all-in-one models match specialists on averages while losing clearly on per-task tail performance, which averages hide.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Quantile-stratified evaluation will show all-in-one models underperforming matched-capacity specialists in the worst-decile inputs of each task, even where mean metrics tie. Falsified if: the all-in-one model matches or exceeds the matched-capacity specialist on the worst-decile (bottom 10% per-input quality) stratum of one or more evaluated tasks.
why_important: Tail performance drives user-perceived reliability; if generalists lose the tail, the all-in-one trend trades invisible-but-real quality for convenience.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Multi-task interference is studied broadly, but tail-focused audits of universal restoration models may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train specialists and an all-in-one model at matched capacity and data per task, then compare full quantile curves rather than means on each task.
main_risk: Capacity matching between one generalist and several specialists is definitionally ambiguous and needs multiple fairness conventions.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Unified restoration models are assumed to benefit from cross-task synergy with negligible interference.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Restoration tasks demand conflicting inverse operators on similar local patterns (sharpen edges versus suppress noise), and conflicts bind hardest where inputs are most ambiguous, which is exactly the tail.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Evaluate one public all-in-one model against one public specialist on the specialist's task, sorting results by difficulty; inspect the hardest examples for a systematic generalist deficit.

one_line_idea: Instruction-based restoration is prompt-fragile: paraphrases of the same enhancement request produce materially different outputs, and no benchmark measures this instability.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Instruction-driven restoration systems accept natural-language requests, and their published results use fixed curated prompts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Output quality and character vary substantially across semantically equivalent phrasings of the same restoration request, so reported results are prompt-tuned upper bounds and real-user experience is systematically worse and inconsistent.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across paraphrase sets of equivalent instructions, output quality will vary by margins comparable to differences between competing methods, and prompt-induced variance will exceed seed-induced variance. Falsified if: prompt-induced output-quality variance is <= seed-induced variance in the variance decomposition across paraphrase sets.
why_important: If prompt variance rivals method differences, instruction-restoration leaderboards are not measuring models but prompt engineering.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Prompt sensitivity is documented for generation; a quantitative instability audit for instruction-based restoration may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build paraphrase sets for canonical restoration requests, run instruction-based systems across them, and decompose output variance into prompt, seed, and input components.
main_risk: Paraphrase equivalence is judgment-dependent; adversarially chosen paraphrases would overstate the effect.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Instruction interfaces are assumed to be robust conveniences layered on stable restoration capability.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Instruction embeddings modulate generation pathways continuously; nothing constrains semantically equivalent phrasings to nearby conditioning vectors, so output equivalence is unenforced.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Run one public instruction-based restorer on one image with several natural paraphrases of the same request and compare outputs; visible quality divergence across phrasings is immediate evidence.

one_line_idea: Generative restoration invalidates images as evidence, and restoration systems for forensic contexts should emit per-region fidelity certificates grounded in observation consistency.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Enhanced images circulate in investigative, legal, and journalistic contexts, while generative restorers can fabricate exactly the details (plates, faces, text) such contexts care about.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A certification layer that decomposes each output region into evidence-supported and prior-injected components, with quantified consistency bounds under the estimated forward model, can be attached to restoration outputs and would change downstream trust decisions in measurable ways.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Certificates validated on synthetic cases will correctly flag most fabricated regions, and user studies with investigators will show materially different reliance decisions when certificates are shown. Falsified if: certificates flag <= 50% of the known-fabricated regions on the synthetic validation cases.
why_important: Society is consuming restored imagery as if it were evidence; an auditable fidelity standard is the difference between a tool and a hazard in these settings.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Uncertainty maps exist in research; an operational certification framework tied to forward-model consistency for forensic consumption may be unbuilt.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define certificate semantics, implement estimation from consistency residuals and sampling dispersion, validate flagging accuracy on synthetic ground truth, and run a decision study with professional users.
main_risk: Certificates could confer unjustified authority if their own error rates are misunderstood, requiring careful calibration reporting.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Restoration quality is treated as a single scalar, with evidentiary reliability considered outside the field's scope.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The information needed for certification (forward-model residuals, posterior dispersion) already exists inside restoration pipelines; discarding it is a choice, not a necessity.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Prototype certificates from cross-seed variance plus re-degradation residuals on synthetic forensic-style cases (plates, documents) and measure how often flagged regions coincide with actual fabrications.

one_line_idea: SR models get amplitude spectra roughly right but phase systematically wrong, and phase error is the better predictor of perceived structural artifacts, motivating phase-aware losses.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Restoration losses operate pointwise or on learned features, without explicit control over how reconstruction error distributes between spectral amplitude and phase, while phase is known to carry structural information in images.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Trained SR models allocate error disproportionately to phase in high frequencies (plausible energy, misplaced structure), phase error correlates with human-perceived structural artifacts better than amplitude error, and adding an explicit phase-coherence term to training reduces structural artifacts at equal amplitude accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Spectral decomposition of errors across models will show phase-dominated high-frequency error, human artifact ratings will track phase error more than amplitude error, and phase-regularized training will improve artifact ratings. Falsified if: in the spectral decomposition of reconstruction error into amplitude and phase components, the phase component accounts for <= 50% of high-frequency error (does not exceed the amplitude component) across the model panel.
why_important: It offers a physically interpretable account of what perceptual losses vaguely address, and a targeted, cheap loss ingredient.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Spectral analyses of GAN artifacts exist; a phase-centric error accounting and phase-targeted loss for SR may be underexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Decompose reconstruction errors of a model panel into amplitude and phase components per band, collect artifact ratings, correlate, then train matched models with and without phase terms.
main_risk: Global Fourier phase is a crude descriptor for local structure, and windowed analyses add parameter choices that affect conclusions.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Spectral amplitude realism is treated as the main frequency-domain target, with phase left implicit.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Pointwise losses are minimized by hedging phase where uncertain, and adversarial losses enforce marginal statistics that constrain amplitude much more than phase alignment with the source.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Swap the phase of model outputs with ground-truth phase (keeping model amplitude) on a few images; a dramatic perceived-quality jump from ground-truth phase alone demonstrates phase is the binding error.

one_line_idea: Blind training over mixed severities teaches models a severity-averaged inverse that is wrong for every severity, and cheap explicit severity conditioning dominates blind averaging.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Blind restoration trains one network over wide severity ranges without telling it the severity, expecting implicit estimation to emerge.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Networks trained blind over mixed severities partially average incompatible inverse operators rather than cleanly inferring severity per input, so an identical network given a coarse severity signal (even a noisy estimate) outperforms the blind version across the entire severity range at matched capacity.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Severity-conditioned models will beat blind models uniformly across the severity axis, and the blind model's per-severity behavior will match a mixture-weighted average of specialists rather than the best specialist per severity. Falsified if: the blind model matches or exceeds the severity-conditioned model of matched capacity at one or more tested severity levels.
why_important: If a one-scalar conditioning input yields uniform gains, the standard blind formulation wastes quality for an unnecessary purity constraint.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Conditioning on degradation parameters exists; characterizing blind training as measurable operator-averaging with a specialist-mixture signature may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train specialists per severity band, a blind model, and a conditioned model at matched capacity; compare per-severity curves and test whether blind behavior matches the specialist mixture prediction.
main_risk: With enough capacity the blind model may internally route severities well, making the effect capacity-dependent.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Blind models are assumed to learn internal severity estimation that approaches conditioned performance.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Severity inference from small receptive fields is uncertain, and under uncertainty the loss-minimizing response is operator averaging; averaging incompatible inverses produces outputs no single severity would want.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Compare one public blind model against the same architecture fine-tuned with an oracle severity input on a severity sweep; a uniform conditioned advantage on the sweep makes the case quickly.

one_line_idea: Overparameterized SR models memorize training patches retrievably: nearest-neighbor probes on outputs would reveal patch-level copying, qualifying texture-generalization claims.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Modern SR models have capacity far exceeding classical estimates of task complexity and train for many epochs over finite patch distributions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable fraction of synthesized high-frequency content in SR outputs consists of near-copies of specific training patches (retrievable by patch-level nearest-neighbor search), concentrated in stochastic texture regions, so texture synthesis is partly patch recall rather than distributional generalization.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Patch-retrieval probes against the training set will find above-chance near-duplicate matches for output texture patches, at rates increasing with model capacity and training epochs and decreasing with training-set size. Falsified if: near-duplicate patch-retrieval match rates for output texture patches are at or below the matched-control (chance) rate.
why_important: Patch recall affects both intellectual-property questions and scientific claims about what SR models learned; it also predicts brittleness on genuinely novel textures.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Memorization probes exist for generative models at the image level; patch-level memorization audits for SR texture synthesis may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Index the training patch corpus, run retrieval on output texture patches versus matched controls (real photos, other models), and quantify near-duplication rates across capacity and data scales.
main_risk: Generic texture similarity produces retrieval hits without memorization, so control baselines and similarity thresholds carry the burden of proof.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] SR texture synthesis is assumed to reflect learned texture statistics rather than recallable instances.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Reconstruction training explicitly rewards reproducing training targets; with excess capacity and repeated exposure, storing high-value patches is the loss-optimal use of parameters.
fastest_falsification_experiment: For one small SR model trained on a modest known corpus, retrieve nearest training patches for its synthesized textures on a few outputs; conspicuous near-duplicates in the first probes demonstrate patch recall.

one_line_idea: Claimed viewpoint invariance of self-supervised ViT features collapses at a measurable camera-baseline knee, and the knee position, not average similarity, predicts a backbone's 3D utility.
problem: Self-supervised 2D features are widely reused for cross-view correspondence and 3D distillation, but the supporting evidence is dominated by narrow-baseline or object-centric pairs.
core_hypothesis: Feature view-invariance is mostly co-visible texture matching and decays nonlinearly with viewpoint change: there is a baseline angle beyond which correspondence utility drops toward chance while narrow-baseline metrics stay high.
falsifiable_prediction: On registered RGB-D scan sequences, reprojection-verified nearest-neighbor match recall for the same 3D points will drop by more than half between the 10-20 degree and 50-60 degree relative-viewpoint bins for frozen SSL ViTs. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if recall at 50-60 degrees is within 20% relative of recall at 10-20 degrees, or if the recall-vs-angle curve shows no knee (max local slope ratio below 2).
why_important: Pose, mapping, and 3D-distillation pipelines budget the number of views assuming smooth feature degradation; a hard knee changes view planning and tells us where 3D-aware fine-tuning should concentrate.
why_possibly_novel: Baseline-stratified correspondence evaluation against ground-truth geometry, with the knee angle reported as a first-class backbone property, does not appear to be a standard published protocol (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample co-visible 3D points from registered indoor scans (e.g., ScanNet-style data), bin image pairs by relative viewpoint angle controlling for co-visibility, and plot feature-match recall at a fixed reprojection threshold versus angle for 3-4 frozen backbones.
main_risk: Occlusion, motion blur, and resolution confound with baseline; co-visibility must be verified from geometry, not assumed.
community_default_belief: Self-supervised ViT features are treated as approximately viewpoint-invariant descriptors whose quality varies smoothly with viewing conditions.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The invariances were learned from 2D crops and photometric augmentations of single images, so genuine out-of-plane rotation is off the training manifold and need not degrade gracefully.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-afternoon: 100 scan image pairs binned by viewpoint angle, one frozen backbone, recall-versus-angle curve from GT-geometry-verified matches.

one_line_idea: Geometric information in vision foundation models peaks in middle transformer blocks, so standard last-layer feature extraction systematically understates and misranks the 3D awareness of 2D backbones.
problem: 3D-awareness probing and feature-lifting pipelines overwhelmingly read features from the final transformer block, inheriting a convention from semantic tasks.
core_hypothesis: Depth, surface-normal, and correspondence information is concentrated in middle blocks and is progressively discarded by later blocks that specialize toward semantic abstraction, and the peak layer shifts with pretraining objective.
falsifiable_prediction: Layer-wise linear probes for monocular depth and normals will peak at 50-75% relative network depth for contrastive and image-text models, with a probe-error gap versus the last layer that exceeds the gap between competing backbones at their respective best layers. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if no middle layer improves depth-probe AbsRel by at least 10% relative over the last layer on both datasets, or if backbone rankings are identical under last-layer and peak-layer protocols.
why_important: If layer choice matters more than backbone choice, published 3D-awareness rankings of foundation models are protocol artifacts and cheap gains are available by re-reading existing checkpoints.
why_possibly_novel: Layer-stratified 3D probing exists for isolated models, but using peak-layer geometry probes to re-rank backbone families and showing rank flips versus last-layer protocol appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Freeze 4-6 public backbones, train identical linear depth and normal probes on every 4th block on one indoor and one outdoor RGB-D dataset, and compare peak-layer versus last-layer probe metrics and cross-backbone rankings.
main_risk: Linear probes may be too weak to expose geometry that is present but nonlinearly encoded, understating late-layer geometry.
community_default_belief: The last layer of a strong foundation model is the best single representation for downstream dense tasks including geometric ones.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Training objectives that reward semantic invariance actively remove pose- and depth-variant information in the final blocks, a loss that semantic benchmarks never detect.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One backbone, probes at 4 layers on one RGB-D dataset, one GPU-day: check whether any middle layer beats the last layer on depth probe error by the kill margin.

one_line_idea: Learned feature upsamplers make features look sharper while corrupting the sub-pixel geometric signal, so pipelines that match or triangulate upsampled features get worse 3D estimates than bilinear baselines.
problem: High-resolution feature upsampling modules are increasingly inserted before geometric uses of foundation features, validated mainly on semantic benchmarks and visual sharpness.
core_hypothesis: Upsamplers trained with image-guided objectives snap feature boundaries to intensity edges, which hallucinates spatial precision: the apparent localization is inherited from the guidance image, not the feature content, and it biases correspondence residuals near depth discontinuities.
falsifiable_prediction: On wide-baseline correspondence with ground-truth geometry, matches from guided-upsampled features will show larger mean epipolar residuals near depth edges than matches from bilinearly upsampled features of the same backbone, despite better-looking feature maps. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if guided upsampling does not increase near-edge median epipolar residual by at least 15% relative in at least 2 of 3 tested upsamplers.
why_important: Sub-pixel accuracy is what SfM, calibration, and reconstruction pipelines actually consume; a component that improves appearance while degrading residuals will silently harm 3D systems as it spreads.
why_possibly_novel: Upsampler evaluation via epipolar and triangulation residuals rather than downstream semantic scores appears untested (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fix one backbone; extract correspondences on standard two-view geometry data via nearest neighbor plus sub-pixel refinement using (a) bilinear and (b) learned guided upsampling; compare epipolar residual distributions stratified by distance to depth edges.
main_risk: Effect may be upsampler-specific; needs 2-3 distinct upsampler designs before a general claim.
community_default_belief: Sharper, edge-aligned feature maps are strictly better inputs for any dense downstream task.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Edge alignment is a semantic prior; geometry lives in phase-like sub-pixel structure that guided filtering overwrites with intensity-edge structure.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a GPU-day: 50 image pairs with GT poses, one backbone, bilinear versus one public upsampler, compare median epipolar residual near depth edges.

one_line_idea: Image-text contrastive features are not geometry-poor: controlling for resolution and probe capacity, their coarse depth-ordering knowledge matches self-supervised features, and the reported gap is a protocol artifact.
problem: The community narrative says contrastive image-text pretraining discards geometry while self-distillation preserves it, based on probe comparisons that differ in resolution, token count, and probe capacity across model families.
core_hypothesis: Much of the measured 3D-awareness gap between image-text and self-distilled backbones is explained by input resolution and effective patch density rather than the pretraining objective.
falsifiable_prediction: After matching effective token grids and probe capacity, the ordinal-depth probe gap between image-text and self-distilled ViTs will shrink by at least half relative to the standard-protocol gap on the same data. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the matched-protocol gap remains above 75% of the standard-protocol gap, confirming the objective-level explanation.
why_important: Objective-level conclusions steer pretraining investments for 3D; if the gap is protocol-induced, cheap resolution interventions matter more than switching objectives.
why_possibly_novel: Resolution-and-capacity-matched 3D probing across objective families, with a variance decomposition into objective versus protocol factors, appears not to have been published (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take paired public checkpoints of comparable size, evaluate ordinal depth-pair accuracy probes at matched token grids and matched probe parameter counts on one indoor and one outdoor dataset, and decompose the gap.
main_risk: Public checkpoints confound objective with data distribution; needs at least one same-data controlled pair to be conclusive.
community_default_belief: Language-supervised pretraining fundamentally sacrifices geometric detail relative to self-supervised visual objectives.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Depth ordering is learnable from monocular pictorial cues that captions weakly but consistently supervise, and probe studies rarely equalize the plumbing that dominates dense readout quality.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: two checkpoints, ordinal depth probes at two matched resolutions each, gap-versus-protocol table.

one_line_idea: Foundation features carry a systematic metric-scale bias inherited from the crop-scale distribution of pretraining augmentations, measurable as a predictable error in apparent-size judgments.
problem: Multi-crop and random-resize augmentations expose models to a specific distribution of object scales, but nobody characterizes what scale prior this stamps into the features.
core_hypothesis: Frozen features encode apparent object scale with a bias toward the pretraining crop-scale distribution: probes estimating physical size or distance will show errors correlated with the mismatch between test-time object scale and the augmentation scale density.
falsifiable_prediction: A size-estimation probe on frozen features will show error that is a U-shaped function of apparent object scale, with the minimum near the modal augmentation scale, consistent across backbones sharing augmentation recipes and shifted for backbones with different recipes. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if probe error curves are flat within noise (max/min bin error ratio below 1.2) or uncorrelated with the documented augmentation scale distributions.
why_important: Scale priors propagate into every metric-3D system built on 2D backbones; knowing the bias direction enables correction layers and better augmentation design for geometry-heavy uses.
why_possibly_novel: Linking augmentation hyperparameters to a quantitative scale-estimation bias curve in downstream probes appears unexplored (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Render controlled scenes with objects at parameterized apparent scales, train size/distance probes on frozen features from backbones with documented augmentation recipes, and regress probe error against distance from the augmentation scale mode.
main_risk: Public models differ in many factors beyond augmentation; a small controlled pretraining run may be needed for causal attribution.
community_default_belief: Augmentation choices affect invariance and semantic quality but wash out as benign implementation details in large-scale pretraining.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Scale is exactly the variable augmentations manipulate most aggressively, so it is the variable most likely to carry a systematic imprint rather than washing out.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two GPU-days: synthetic renders across 8 scale bins, two backbones with different documented crop policies, probe-error-versus-scale curves.

one_line_idea: Under controlled synthetic viewpoint sweeps, generative-diffusion features are not more multi-view consistent than contrastive features once texture density is controlled, contradicting a growing assumption in 3D distillation work.
problem: A popular assumption holds that features from generative models are more 3D-consistent because generation requires implicit geometry, but comparisons are made on uncontrolled real images.
core_hypothesis: Apparent cross-view stability advantages of diffusion features come from their sensitivity to low-frequency appearance, which correlates across views for texture-poor content, not from superior geometric encoding.
falsifiable_prediction: On rendered viewpoint sweeps of textured versus texture-poor assets, the cross-view feature stability advantage of diffusion features over contrastive features will appear only in texture-poor conditions and vanish or invert for high-texture assets at matched spatial resolution. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if diffusion features hold a stability advantage of at least 10% relative in both texture bins, which would support the community belief.
why_important: Choice of 2D teacher for 3D feature fields and correspondence distillation is being made on this belief; a texture-confound explanation changes teacher selection and hybrid strategies.
why_possibly_novel: Texture-controlled synthetic viewpoint-sweep evaluation of feature families with a stability-by-texture interaction analysis appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Render viewpoint orbits of public 3D assets stratified by texture statistics, compute view-pair feature similarity for matched 3D surface points across feature families, and test the family-by-texture interaction.
main_risk: Rendered imagery may be out-of-distribution for both families in ways that reorder them; a small real multi-view control set is needed.
community_default_belief: Generative pretraining yields features with better 3D consistency than discriminative or contrastive pretraining.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Generation quality mostly requires local appearance modeling; cross-view identity of surface points is never directly supervised in either family, so neither has a principled advantage.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 50 assets in two texture bins, two feature families, view-pair cosine similarity at GT-corresponding points, interaction test.

one_line_idea: A measurable fraction of reported 3D awareness in ViT probes is absolute positional-embedding leakage: probes read where a patch is in the frame, not what geometry the features encode.
problem: Depth and normal probes on frozen ViTs are interpreted as measuring geometric content of learned features, but ViT tokens also carry absolute position information that correlates with depth in typical photographs (ground below, sky above).
core_hypothesis: A nontrivial share of probe performance survives feature ablation but not position ablation, meaning current 3D-awareness numbers overstate the geometry actually encoded in appearance features.
falsifiable_prediction: Depth probes re-evaluated under vertical-flip test-time transforms and randomized crop offsets will lose a disproportionate share of accuracy compared to semantic probes on the same tokens, and a position-only baseline probe will explain a nontrivial fraction of reported depth-probe skill. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the position-only probe explains under 10% of full-probe depth accuracy and position randomization changes probe error by under 5% relative.
why_important: 3D-awareness leaderboards inform which backbones get lifted into 3D pipelines; if position leakage inflates scores, rankings and conclusions about pretraining objectives are distorted.
why_possibly_novel: Position-only baselines and position-randomization controls appear absent from published 3D-awareness probing protocols (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: For 3 backbones, train (a) standard depth probes, (b) probes on position-randomized tokens, and (c) position-only probes with no image content, on one indoor and one outdoor dataset; decompose probe skill into content and position components.
main_risk: Aggressive position randomization can degrade features themselves, over-attributing skill to position; needs careful crop-based controls.
community_default_belief: Probe accuracy on frozen features measures the geometric information content of the learned representation.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Natural image composition makes vertical position alone a strong depth predictor, and probes will exploit any shortcut available.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a GPU-day: position-only probe on one dataset; if it reaches a substantial fraction of full-probe skill the leakage concern is live.

one_line_idea: Textureless-surface correspondence failure of foundation features is a token-granularity artifact, and dense overlapping-stride re-extraction recovers most of it without any retraining.
problem: Feature-based matching is believed to fail intrinsically on textureless surfaces, pushing systems toward expensive learned matchers or active sensing.
core_hypothesis: Much of the failure is quantization: coarse patch grids average away weak shading gradients that do carry correspondence signal, so densely re-extracting features with overlapping strides and aggregating them recovers usable matches on low-texture regions.
falsifiable_prediction: On low-texture regions of multi-view stereo benchmarks with GT geometry, overlapping-stride aggregation of the same frozen backbone will raise reprojection-verified match recall substantially over standard single-stride extraction, at unchanged model weights. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if low-texture match recall improves by under 25% relative, or if accepted-match triangulation error worsens by more than 10%.
why_important: A zero-training recipe that extends frozen-feature matching into low-texture regions widens where cheap 2D backbones can replace engineered matchers in reconstruction and localization.
why_possibly_novel: Stride-aggregation is known for semantic sharpness, but its effect on low-texture geometric matching measured by reprojection recall appears uncharacterized (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Select low-texture regions via local contrast statistics on standard MVS scenes, run matching from single-stride versus shifted-stride-aggregated features, and compare recall at fixed reprojection thresholds and triangulation error of accepted matches.
main_risk: Compute grows with stride density, and aggregation may blur across depth edges, trading one failure for another.
community_default_belief: Textureless regions carry too little photometric signal for passive feature matching, regardless of extraction details.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Shading varies smoothly but measurably across most matte surfaces; the signal exists below the patch-grid Nyquist limit and is destroyed by coarse tokenization rather than absent.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 20 low-texture scene pairs, stride-1/4-offset aggregation versus baseline, recall-at-threshold comparison.

one_line_idea: Decomposing 2D features into view-invariant and view-dependent components before lifting them into 3D feature fields yields more geometrically faithful fields than the standard practice of averaging raw features across views.
problem: 3D feature fields are built by averaging multi-view 2D features per 3D point, silently mixing view-dependent components (lighting, specular response, occlusion context) into a representation treated as view-invariant.
core_hypothesis: A per-scene low-rank decomposition separating features into a view-independent term plus a small view-conditioned residual will reduce cross-view inconsistency of the lifted field and improve geometry-sensitive downstream readouts without new pretraining.
falsifiable_prediction: Fields built with the decomposition will improve 3D point re-identification accuracy across held-out views and reduce feature-field gradient noise near smooth surfaces, compared to mean-aggregated fields from identical inputs. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if held-out-view point re-identification improves by under 5% relative on 4 of 5 scenes.
why_important: Feature fields are becoming the interface between 2D foundation models and 3D reasoning; a principled aggregation fix improves every consumer of that interface at low cost.
why_possibly_novel: View-dependence-aware aggregation is standard for radiance but appears unexamined for lifted semantic features, where mean pooling remains default (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: On multi-view scenes with GT geometry, lift features by (a) per-point mean and (b) low-rank view-decomposed aggregation; evaluate held-out-view point re-identification and consistency of field values at GT-corresponding points.
main_risk: The decomposition may absorb genuine semantic variation into the view-dependent term, diluting semantics; needs a semantic retrieval control.
community_default_belief: Averaging 2D features across registered views is an adequate estimator of a point's canonical descriptor.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Features are trained on single images and demonstrably carry illumination and context signatures; averaging biased samples yields a biased canonical descriptor, especially with few or clustered views.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 5 scenes, rank-1 view-dependent term, held-out-view re-identification delta.

one_line_idea: Jointly distilling 2D semantic features into Gaussian-splat scenes measurably degrades the recovered geometry relative to photometric-only optimization, a cost the feature-field literature does not report.
problem: Feature-distilled 3D Gaussian scenes are evaluated on semantic utility and rendering quality, while effects on the underlying geometry are rarely quantified.
core_hypothesis: Feature-rendering losses reward placing primitives where 2D features are stable rather than where surfaces are, systematically biasing Gaussian positions and opacities and worsening depth and surface accuracy versus photometric-only baselines.
falsifiable_prediction: On scenes with GT geometry, adding standard feature-distillation losses will worsen rendered-depth error and surface chamfer distance relative to photometric-only training at matched primitive budgets and iterations. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if geometry degradation is under 5% relative on all metrics across the loss-weight sweep, indicating the tax is negligible.
why_important: Feature-augmented 3D scenes are being adopted as maps for robotics and AR where geometric accuracy is the point; an unreported geometry tax changes the design tradeoff.
why_possibly_novel: Geometry-side ablations of feature distillation (depth error, chamfer, normal error) appear absent from the feature-field literature, which reports semantic metrics (unverified).

one_line_idea: Foundation features cannot disambiguate the front and back of near-symmetric objects, and the error direction is predicted by canonical-pose frequency in web imagery, making pose pipelines built on them systematically biased rather than randomly wrong.
problem: Object pose estimation increasingly bootstraps from foundation-feature matching, but symmetry-related failures are treated as noise instead of being characterized.
core_hypothesis: For objects with approximate front-back symmetry, feature matching resolves the ambiguity by defaulting to the pose most frequent in web photos, producing structured 180-degree errors whose frequency tracks canonical-pose bias rather than image evidence.
falsifiable_prediction: On rendered symmetric-object pose tasks, the distribution of 180-degree flip errors will correlate with an independent estimate of view-frequency bias per category, and flips will persist even when disambiguating cues are clearly visible. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the flip-rate/view-frequency rank correlation is below 0.4, or if visible disambiguating cues reduce flips below 5% (bias absent).
why_important: Structured bias is fixable (priors can be subtracted, cues can be reweighted) while random noise is not; robotics grasping and AR anchoring need to know which one they face.
why_possibly_novel: Attributing symmetry-flip statistics to web view-frequency priors, with a quantitative correlation, appears untested (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Render pose-estimation probes for symmetric assets with controlled disambiguating cues, run feature-matching-based pose estimation, and correlate flip rates with view-frequency statistics estimated from a public image corpus per category.
main_risk: View-frequency estimation from a corpus is itself noisy; needs a robustness check across corpora.
community_default_belief: Pose errors on symmetric objects are irreducible ambiguity noise inherent to the object, not a model-specific bias.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The models were trained on a heavily biased distribution of object views, and ambiguity resolution under bias defaults to the prior, which is measurable and correctable.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 20 categories, rendered flip-rate versus corpus view-frequency correlation.

one_line_idea: The believed semantics-versus-geometry fine-tuning tradeoff in foundation backbones is a protocol artifact: tuning only late blocks at small learning rates buys large geometry gains at near-zero semantic cost.
problem: Teams keep backbones frozen for 3D tasks because fine-tuning is believed to catastrophically erode semantic quality, forcing adapter complexity into every 3D pipeline.
core_hypothesis: The reported tradeoff comes from full-network tuning at semantic-task learning rates; geometry-relevant capacity is concentrated in late blocks whose careful tuning improves depth and correspondence probes while leaving semantic retrieval essentially intact.
falsifiable_prediction: A last-25%-of-blocks tuning schedule on a geometry objective will improve depth-probe error and correspondence recall by a large margin over frozen features while semantic retrieval and linear classification drop by only a small margin, across at least two backbone families. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if every schedule that improves depth-probe AbsRel by 15% relative also costs more than 3% absolute semantic retrieval accuracy.
why_important: If true, the field can stop paying the adapter tax and ship single backbones that serve both semantic and geometric consumers.
why_possibly_novel: Block-stratified tuning studies exist for semantics, but a geometry-objective tuning frontier mapped jointly against semantic retention appears missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sweep tuned-block fraction and learning rate on a multi-view geometry objective; measure the joint frontier of depth-probe AbsRel, correspondence recall, and semantic retrieval accuracy versus the frozen baseline.
main_risk: The frontier may be data-dependent; requires indoor and outdoor training mixes to check stability.
community_default_belief: Fine-tuning a foundation backbone on geometric objectives destroys its general-purpose semantic value, so freezing is mandatory.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Catastrophic forgetting scales with how much of the network moves; the belief was set by full-tuning experiments and never re-checked with surgical schedules on geometry objectives.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two GPU-days: one backbone, 3 tuned-block fractions, joint geometry/semantic metric table.

one_line_idea: Monocular depth foundation models infer focal length implicitly from image content, and their metric-depth errors are largely explained by the error of that hidden focal estimate.
problem: Metric monocular depth models are deployed on images with unknown intrinsics, yet their error structure is reported as scene-level statistics with no accounting of the intrinsics-inference component.
core_hypothesis: These models contain an implicit focal-length estimator driven by content cues (face sizes, room proportions, edge convergence), and metric-depth error decomposes into a dominant multiplicative term tracking hidden focal error plus a smaller residual.
falsifiable_prediction: Re-rendering the same scenes at multiple focal lengths will produce depth errors that are predictable from a focal-estimation probe on the model's intermediate features, with the multiplicative error component explaining most of the variance in metric AbsRel across focal conditions. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the focal-linked multiplicative component explains under 30% of metric AbsRel variance across the sweep.
why_important: If focal inference dominates metric error, supplying or estimating intrinsics separately fixes most of the problem, redirecting effort away from bigger depth decoders.
why_possibly_novel: Decomposing metric-depth error into implicit-focal error plus residual via controlled focal re-rendering appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Render or crop-zoom real scenes across a focal sweep with fixed GT depth, evaluate a metric depth model, probe intermediate features for focal estimates, and regress depth error against probed focal error.
main_risk: Crop-zoom changes composition cues as well as intrinsics; needs true re-rendering or careful field-of-view controls.
community_default_belief: Metric depth models learn depth end-to-end, and intrinsics sensitivity is one unstructured error source among many.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Metric depth from a single image is mathematically impossible without an intrinsics assumption, so the model must be making one internally, and internal estimates have measurable, structured errors.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: synthetic focal sweep on 20 scenes, error-versus-focal curve plus feature probe.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: camera focal length at fixed scene

one_line_idea: Generalization of monocular depth models scales with scene-layout diversity of training data, not raw image count, and layout-diversity-matched subsets can replicate full-data performance at a fraction of the size.
problem: Depth model training mixes keep growing, but there is no controlled account of which data property actually buys cross-domain generalization.
core_hypothesis: Cross-domain depth error is governed by coverage of scene-layout statistics (depth-range distribution, openness, clutter) rather than image count; beyond layout coverage saturation, additional images yield negligible gains.
falsifiable_prediction: Training identical architectures on (a) random subsets and (b) layout-diversity-stratified subsets of the same pool will show the stratified subsets matching full-pool cross-domain AbsRel at severalfold smaller size, while random subsets of equal size lag. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if diversity-stratified subsets beat random subsets by under 5% relative cross-domain AbsRel at equal size.
why_important: Data acquisition and licensing dominate the cost of depth foundation models; a validated diversity criterion converts data curation from folklore to measurement.
why_possibly_novel: Depth-specific data-scaling analyses controlling for layout statistics rather than dataset identity appear missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define layout descriptors from GT depth statistics, construct matched-size random versus diversity-stratified training subsets, train identical models, and evaluate on held-out domains.
main_risk: Layout descriptors may miss the true governing property (materials, lighting), yielding a false negative on the specific descriptor set rather than on the diversity thesis.
community_default_belief: More images monotonically improve depth generalization, so scale is the primary lever.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Depth error concentrates on layout regimes absent from training; duplicating well-covered regimes adds nothing, which is invisible in aggregate metrics but decisive under stratified evaluation.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three GPU-days: two subset policies at one size on one public pool, cross-domain AbsRel comparison.

one_line_idea: Teacher-student pseudo-label distillation, the engine of current depth foundation models, systematically erodes depth discontinuities with each generation, measurable as monotonic depth-edge degradation across distillation rounds.
problem: Pseudo-label distillation on unlabeled images is credited for depth generalization gains, with quality reported via global metrics that barely weight discontinuities.
core_hypothesis: Averaging effects in teacher ensembling and student regression act as an edge low-pass filter: each distillation generation smooths depth discontinuities further, degrading edge localization while global AbsRel improves or holds.
falsifiable_prediction: Across successive distillation generations of the same pipeline, depth-boundary localization error on edge-annotated benchmarks will increase monotonically while global AbsRel does not, and the effect will scale with the amount of pseudo-labeled data. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if edge-localization error grows by under 5% relative per generation, or if it improves, across two generations.
why_important: Edges are what grasping, occlusion reasoning, and compositing consume; a hidden edge tax means the flagship training recipe optimizes the wrong thing for key consumers.
why_possibly_novel: Generation-stratified edge-metric audits of distillation pipelines appear unreported; papers compare endpoint models only (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Re-run a public distillation recipe for 2-3 generations at reduced scale, evaluating each generation on depth-edge completeness and localization metrics alongside global error on edge-annotated depth data.
main_risk: Small-scale reruns may not reproduce large-scale dynamics; conclusions need a scale-sensitivity caveat.
community_default_belief: Pseudo-label distillation is a near-free way to convert unlabeled images into depth performance, with quality summarized by global error metrics.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Regression to soft targets provably shrinks high-frequency components under label noise, and depth edges are exactly the high-frequency, high-disagreement pixels.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two GPU-days: one distillation generation versus its teacher on an edge-annotated benchmark, edge-localization delta.

problem: Relative depth is described as essentially solved because whole-image ordinal accuracy is high, yet downstream failures (AR occlusion glitches, wrong support relations) persist.
core_hypothesis: Remaining ordinal errors are not uniformly distributed but concentrate at pixel pairs spanning object-ground contact and support boundaries, where pictorial cues are ambiguous; aggregate ordinal metrics dilute these decisive pairs.
falsifiable_prediction: Constructing pair-sampling protocols focused on contact regions from existing GT depth will show ordinal accuracy dropping far below the whole-image figure for the same state-of-the-art models, with consistent error direction (objects fused to ground). KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if contact-stratified ordinal accuracy is within 5 points of generic-pair accuracy for both models.
why_important: Contact relations drive occlusion, support, and physical plausibility reasoning; knowing that they are the residual failure redirects both training data and evaluation design.
why_possibly_novel: Contact-stratified ordinal evaluation of modern relative-depth models appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: From existing RGB-D datasets, sample ordinal pairs stratified as contact-spanning versus generic, evaluate public relative-depth models, and compare stratified ordinal accuracies and error directions.
main_risk: Contact regions have higher GT depth noise in consumer RGB-D data; needs sensor-noise-aware filtering.
community_default_belief: Relative depth ranking is a solved capability, with remaining errors being unstructured residual noise.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Monocular contact cues (shadows, occlusion boundaries) are exactly the cues that web-scale photography renders inconsistent, so models plausibly never learned them reliably; aggregate metrics cannot see it.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a GPU-day: 2k contact-spanning pairs from one RGB-D dataset, two public models, stratified ordinal accuracy.

one_line_idea: Detected object instances of known physical size classes act as an implicit calibration rig: a post-hoc scale solver over class-size priors converts relative depth to metric depth competitively with intrinsics-aware models on populated scenes.
problem: Metric depth is gated on knowing camera intrinsics or training metric heads per camera family, blocking deployment on arbitrary web and archival imagery.
core_hypothesis: For scenes containing common object classes, a robust joint solve over class-size distributions and a global scale-shift transform yields metric depth whose accuracy approaches intrinsics-conditioned models, because size priors over multiple instances over-constrain the scale.
falsifiable_prediction: On populated indoor and street scenes, prior-solved metric depth from a relative-depth backbone will land within a modest factor of intrinsics-aware baselines in scale-error percentiles, and accuracy will improve predictably with the number of detected known-size instances. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if median absolute scale error exceeds 20% even for scenes with 5+ known-size instances.
why_important: It unlocks metric 3D from uncalibrated single images at scale, and quantifies exactly when object priors substitute for calibration.
why_possibly_novel: Object-size priors have been used ad hoc; a characterized, uncertainty-weighted solver with instance-count scaling laws appears missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build the solver over public class-size statistics, run on RGB-D scenes stratified by known-size instance count, and report scale-error distribution versus instance count against an intrinsics-aware baseline.
main_risk: Class-size variance (children versus adults, chair types) may leave irreducible scale noise; the scaling curve versus instance count is the diagnostic.
community_default_belief: Metric scale from a single uncalibrated image is unreliable folklore, acceptable only as a rough heuristic.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Scale error from size priors averages down with independent instances roughly as root-n, so populated scenes can beat the single-cue intuition the folklore is based on.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 100 populated scenes, solver versus GT scale, error-versus-instance-count curve.

one_line_idea: Depth foundation models fail on non-pinhole imagery with a characteristic radial error signature, and a lens-conditioned resampling wrapper recovers most of the loss without retraining the backbone.
problem: Fisheye, action-camera, and panoramic imagery is pervasive, yet depth models are trained and evaluated almost exclusively on near-pinhole projections.
core_hypothesis: On distorted projections these models produce errors that are a deterministic function of radial position (depth bowing tracking local focal-length variation), implying the failure is a projection mismatch rather than a representation gap, and is correctable by projection-aware resampling.
falsifiable_prediction: Error-versus-image-radius curves on real fisheye captures will show a monotone radial bias consistent across scenes and models, and piecewise-pinhole resampling before inference will remove most of the radial component of AbsRel. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the radial error component is under 10% of total AbsRel on raw fisheye inputs, meaning the problem is negligible.
why_important: A projection wrapper is orders cheaper than retraining foundation models per lens family, and the radial signature diagnoses when it suffices.
why_possibly_novel: Radius-stratified error decomposition of depth foundation models on real wide-angle lenses, with a resampling-recovery bound, appears unreported (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Capture or reuse calibrated fisheye RGB-D data, evaluate public depth models raw versus after piecewise-pinhole resampling, and report radial error profiles and recovery fractions.
main_risk: Resampling introduces interpolation artifacts and field-of-view seams that may add their own error floor.
community_default_belief: Depth models generalize across cameras, and distortion is a minor preprocessing detail handled by undistortion when intrinsics happen to be known.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The perspective-scale cues these models rely on vary with local focal length across a distorted image, so the failure is structural and spatially systematic, not minor.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a GPU-day: one calibrated fisheye RGB-D set, radial error profile raw versus resampled.

one_line_idea: Restricting test-time adaptation of video depth to per-sequence scale-shift-bias parameters under multi-view photometric consistency gives robust cross-domain gains where full-model TTA collapses.
problem: Test-time adaptation for depth is considered unstable because photometric self-supervision at test time can degrade the model catastrophically on hard sequences.
core_hypothesis: Instability comes from adapting high-capacity weights on a biased self-supervised signal; constraining adaptation to a handful of affine parameters per sequence keeps the photometric signal identifiable and converts TTA from risky to reliably positive.
falsifiable_prediction: On cross-domain video sequences with GT depth, affine-only TTA will improve AbsRel on a clear majority of sequences with bounded worst-case degradation, while full-decoder TTA under the identical loss shows heavy-tailed failures. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if affine-only TTA fails to improve median AbsRel by at least 5% relative, or if its worst-decile degradation exceeds 3% relative.
why_important: A safe TTA recipe converts every deployed depth system into one that self-corrects domain shift without fleet retraining, and the capacity-stability tradeoff generalizes to other dense regressors.
why_possibly_novel: Capacity-stratified stability analysis of photometric TTA (affine versus decoder versus full) with worst-case guarantees appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement photometric-consistency TTA at three capacity tiers on cross-domain driving and handheld sequences, and report per-sequence AbsRel delta distributions including worst-decile behavior.
main_risk: Affine capacity may be too small to fix structured errors (edges, thin objects), capping the achievable gain.
community_default_belief: Test-time photometric adaptation of depth models is too unstable for production use.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The instability evidence conflates adaptation signal quality with adaptation capacity; a 4-parameter update cannot collapse a network and the photometric signal is sufficient to fit 4 parameters.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: 30 cross-domain sequences, affine versus full TTA, per-sequence delta histogram.

problem: Depth models degrade in low light, and the degradation is treated as irreducible noise motivating sensor fusion or heavy retraining.
core_hypothesis: Under low light, depth errors are mostly systematic (global underestimation of range and compression of far-field structure) and predictable from exposure statistics, so a small correction module conditioned on exposure features can restore a large fraction of accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: Error decomposition on paired day/night or bracketed-exposure captures will attribute the majority of added AbsRel to a low-dimensional bias field, and a correction head with under 1% of backbone parameters will recover more than half of the low-light degradation. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill if the structured bias component explains under 40% of low-light AbsRel increase, or the correction head recovers under 30%.
why_important: Night operation is where depth failures are costly; a near-free correction beats both expensive retraining and added sensors for many applications.
why_possibly_novel: Bias/variance decomposition of low-light depth error with an exposure-conditioned correction bound appears unreported (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use datasets with day/night or exposure-bracketed geometry-paired captures, fit the low-dimensional bias model per condition, train the correction head on one domain, and test recovery on held-out scenes.
main_risk: Sensor noise at extreme darkness may genuinely raise variance, capping recoverable error below the target.
community_default_belief: Low-light depth failure reflects missing information in the image and can only be fixed with better sensors or large-scale night training data.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Much of the failure may be a domain-prior mismatch (models calibrated to daytime luminance statistics), which is a correctable bias, not missing information.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: exposure-bracketed set, bias-field fit, fraction-of-error-explained statistic.

one_line_idea: Small-baseline temporal parallax in casual video contains enough signal to resolve metric scale without IMU or intrinsics, and current video depth models fail to exploit it, as revealed by a parallax-ablation test.
problem: Video depth models are marketed as temporally consistent, but it is unknown whether they actually use inter-frame parallax as a geometric signal or merely smooth per-frame predictions.
core_hypothesis: Handheld jitter provides usable metric parallax; models trained with explicit multi-frame geometric losses can recover absolute scale from it, while current systems show near-zero sensitivity to parallax ablation, proving they ignore the signal.
falsifiable_prediction: Synthetically freezing camera translation (temporal replication with matched noise) will leave current video-depth outputs nearly unchanged, while a parallax-aware model will degrade on scale metrics when parallax is removed and beat single-frame baselines on metric error when it is present. KILL THRESHOLD (pre-registered): Kill the capability claim if the parallax-aware prototype reduces median scale error by under 20% relative to its single-frame twin on jittery sequences.
why_important: Free metric scale from casual video would remove the calibration bottleneck for consumer 3D applications; the ablation also gives the field a clean test of whether temporal models do geometry or smoothing.
why_possibly_novel: The parallax-ablation sensitivity test as a published diagnostic, and a metric-from-jitter capability claim quantified against it, appear new (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate public video-depth models on sequences with GT metric depth under real versus parallax-ablated inputs; train a small multi-frame model with an explicit two-view metric loss and compare scale-error sensitivity.
main_risk: Rolling-shutter and motion blur may corrupt the tiny-baseline signal below usability on real footage.
community_default_belief: Casual handheld video lacks sufficient baseline for metric depth, so scale must come from IMU, intrinsics, or learned priors.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Centimeter-level jitter at typical scene depths yields parallax well above modern sub-pixel matching accuracy, so the information is present and simply unexploited.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: parallax-ablation sensitivity of two public video-depth models on 20 GT sequences.
