one_line_idea: Resolution-extrapolation recipes for dense inference: a position-encoding rescaling law plus attention-temperature correction lets models trained at 512px infer at 2048px with minimal degradation, unlocking high-resolution deployment without high-resolution training.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Dense models degrade when inferring far above training resolution, and the standard remedies (multi-crop tiling or high-resolution finetuning) cost either context integrity or significant compute.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most extrapolation degradation in ViT-based dense models comes from two quantifiable shifts — position-encoding interpolation distortion and attention-entropy growth with token count — both of which admit closed-form corrections (log-linear PE rescaling; temperature scaled by log token count), so corrected models extrapolate gracefully without finetuning.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Cityscapes with a SegFormer/ViT model trained at 512px, corrected whole-image 2048px inference will retain at least 95% of native-resolution mIoU, versus at most 88% for naive extrapolation, and each correction will contribute measurably in ablation (at least 2 mIoU together); kill the idea if naive extrapolation already retains over 93% (nothing to fix) or corrections add under 1.0 mIoU (wrong mechanism).
why_important: High-resolution inference without tiling preserves global context for large scenes, and a training-free recipe is immediately adoptable by anyone deploying frozen dense models.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] PE interpolation and attention-entropy corrections circulate in language-model context extension; a validated dense-vision extrapolation recipe with mechanism-level ablations appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate whole-image inference at 1x/2x/4x training resolution with each correction toggled, on Cityscapes and ADE20K, and correlate degradation with measured attention-entropy shift per layer.
main_risk: Convolutional components (in hybrid heads) have their own resolution pathologies that these token-level corrections do not address, capping retention regardless.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Resolution extrapolation is assumed to require finetuning or tiling, and inference resolution is pinned to training resolution as a rule of practice.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Degradation may be dominated by scale mismatch between object sizes seen at training and test, a data-statistics issue no encoding correction can fix.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference-only sweeps with public MMSegmentation checkpoints on Cityscapes and ADE20K run in under 6 hours on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Annotation-convention directions in weight space: interpolating between checkpoints finetuned on two mask conventions traces a monotone boundary-style continuum, giving deployment-time convention control from a single stored direction vector.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Models must commit to one annotation convention at training time, and serving users with different convention needs requires separate checkpoints.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because convention differences are a systematic low-complexity output transformation, the weight-space displacement between same-base checkpoints finetuned under two conventions acts as a convention direction: interpolation coefficients map monotonically onto boundary-style statistics, making the direction a control knob rather than a lottery.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Interpolating between COCO-convention and LVIS-convention finetunes of one base Mask2Former, boundary-tightness statistics of the outputs will vary monotonically with the coefficient (Spearman rho at least 0.9 across 11 steps), and the midpoint model will score within 1.5 mask-AP of convention-specific models when evaluated under a synthetic mid-convention reference; kill the idea if interpolation is non-monotone or midpoint quality collapses by over 5 AP (loss barrier), meaning conventions are not linearly connected.
why_important: One stored direction replacing per-convention checkpoints is a practical serving capability and evidence that label conventions occupy structured weight-space directions, a reusable scientific finding.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Weight interpolation between finetunes is studied for accuracy-robustness tradeoffs; convention control as the interpolation axis with a monotonicity kill test appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Finetune one base under each convention on the dual-annotated COCO/LVIS overlap, sweep interpolation, and measure boundary-tightness monotonicity plus AP under both conventions at each step.
main_risk: The two finetunes may drift apart in unrelated directions (data order, augmentation), burying the convention signal inside a noisy displacement vector.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Weight interpolation between differently supervised models is expected to produce loss barriers, not controllable intermediate behavior.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Convention differences may be too category-idiosyncratic for one global direction to express, showing monotonicity on average but incoherence per class.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two Mask2Former finetunes on the public COCO/LVIS dual-annotation overlap plus interpolation sweeps run in about 1.5 days on one A100; all public.

one_line_idea: Procrustes head transplants: aligning feature spaces with an orthogonal map fitted on unlabeled images lets a task head trained on an old backbone run on a new backbone, recovering most performance with zero task-label retraining.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Backbone upgrades orphan every trained task head, and retraining heads requires task labels and compute that many deployments no longer have access to.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense feature spaces of successive backbone generations are related by an approximately orthogonal transformation identifiable from unlabeled data alone (matching feature statistics on shared images), so head transplantation via Procrustes alignment recovers most task performance, with the residual gap measuring genuinely new information in the upgraded backbone.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Transplanting a detection head trained on DINOv2 ViT-B features onto DINOv2 ViT-L (and onto OpenCLIP ViT-B) via orthogonal alignment fitted on 5k unlabeled COCO images will recover at least 70% of the box AP that full head retraining on the new backbone achieves; kill the idea if recovery is under 40% for the within-family transplant, meaning even sibling feature spaces are not orthogonally alignable at dense granularity.
why_important: Zero-label backbone upgrades are a deployment capability with immediate value wherever labels are private, expired, or expensive, and the recovery fraction is a clean measure of representational continuity across model generations.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Model stitching uses trained adapters with labels; label-free orthogonal transplantation for dense heads with a recovery benchmark appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit orthogonal maps between backbone pairs on unlabeled images, transplant frozen detection/segmentation heads, and compare against label-based head retraining and no-alignment controls on COCO and ADE20K.
main_risk: Orthogonality is a strong constraint; if the true relation involves scaling and subspace reweighting, recovery may hinge on relaxations that require labels to fit, undermining the zero-label story.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Head retraining after backbone changes is treated as unavoidable, with feature spaces assumed incompatibly reorganized across generations.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Detection heads consume multi-scale features whose cross-backbone correspondence may be layer-permuted, breaking any single-layer alignment scheme.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Alignment fitting (hours, unlabeled) plus inference evaluations and one reference Faster R-CNN head retraining (DINOv2 backbones) on COCO subsets take about 2 days on one A100; all checkpoints and data public.

one_line_idea: Dense-task finetuning edits are layer-sparse: most of a task vector's effect concentrates in a small fraction of layers, so sparse task-delta storage and merging preserve capability at a fifth of the memory and interference cost.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Task vectors are stored and merged as full-model deltas, and merging many tasks accumulates interference across all layers simultaneously.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense-task adaptation is functionally localized: a small subset of layers (late blocks and decoder interfaces) carries nearly all task-relevant change, so truncating task vectors to their top-energy layers preserves single-task performance and reduces multi-task merge interference because deltas overlap less.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] For detection and segmentation finetunes of a shared ViT base, task vectors truncated to the top 20% of layers by delta energy will retain at least 95% of full-delta task performance, and three-task merges of truncated vectors will beat full-vector merges by at least 1.5 points average; kill the idea if truncation to 20% of layers loses over 15% of single-task performance, meaning dense adaptation is functionally distributed.
why_important: Establishes a locality law for dense-task adaptation that directly enables cheaper checkpoint logistics and better merging, tying a scientific claim to an operational payoff.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Delta sparsification appears in NLP merging work; a layer-level locality characterization for dense perception tasks with merge-interference consequences appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Compute per-layer delta energies for public dense finetunes, evaluate truncated-delta models across energy thresholds, and run three-task merges (detection, semantic, keypoints) under full vs truncated deltas.
main_risk: Delta energy may mislocate functional importance (small deltas in sensitive layers matter more), requiring causal layer-patching controls that complicate the story.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Finetuning is assumed to spread task information diffusely across all layers, making full deltas the safe default.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Layer sparsity may hold for heads-adjacent layers trivially while the claimed backbone locality fails, reducing the finding to the obvious.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Using public finetuned checkpoints (MMDetection/MMSegmentation ViT-based) plus truncation and merge evaluations on COCO/ADE20K subsets takes about 1 day on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Pre-merge orthogonalization: projecting task vectors to reduce their pairwise conflict before merging recovers a large share of the performance lost to interference, turning merge quality from a lottery into a controlled procedure.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Multi-task weight merging loses performance as tasks are added, and existing remedies (sign election, magnitude pruning) treat symptoms without an explicit interference model.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Merge degradation is dominated by conflicting components of task vectors in a low-dimensional shared subspace; orthogonalizing task vectors against each other's high-curvature directions (estimated from cheap Fisher approximations) before averaging removes the destructive interference while keeping each task's private components, recovering most of the specialist gap.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Merging three dense-task specialists (semantic segmentation, detection, human keypoints) from a shared ViT base, Fisher-guided orthogonalization will recover at least 50% of the average per-task gap between naive task-arithmetic merging and individual specialists, and beat TIES-style sign election by at least 1.0 point average; kill the idea if recovery over naive merging is under 20%, meaning interference is not subspace-structured.
why_important: A working interference model upgrades merging from heuristic to engineering discipline, enabling one-checkpoint deployment of perception suites on edge systems.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sign-election and pruning heuristics exist (TIES lineage); explicit curvature-guided orthogonalization for dense perception merges with a recovery-fraction kill line appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Finetune three specialists from one base, estimate diagonal/low-rank Fisher per task on 1k images each, orthogonalize and merge under several projection strengths, and compare per-task metrics against naive, TIES, and specialist references.
main_risk: Cheap Fisher approximations may misidentify the conflict subspace, and the projection could remove task-critical components exactly for the most distinctive task.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Merge interference is treated as an unavoidable tax, with per-task adapters seen as the only reliable multi-task deployment path.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Interference may be intrinsically high-rank for dense tasks, in which case no projection preserves all tasks and adapters remain strictly better.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three specialist finetunes (ViT-B UPerNet / Faster R-CNN / ViTPose-style head) on COCO/ADE20K subsets plus merge sweeps run in about 4 days on one A100; all models and data public.

one_line_idea: Permutation-aligned merging of independently trained dense models: re-basin alignment extends from classifiers to segmentation networks, enabling federated-style averaging of models trained by different parties without shared initialization.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Weight averaging fails across independently initialized trainings due to permutation symmetry, and re-basin alignment has been demonstrated mainly on classifiers; dense-prediction models with skip connections and decoders remain untested territory.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Permutation alignment generalizes to encoder-decoder segmentation networks when alignment respects skip-connection coupling constraints (aligned units must permute consistently across the skip), so two independently trained DeepLab/UNet-style models can be averaged into a working model near the loss barrier-free regime.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Aligning and averaging two independently trained DeepLabv3+ models on Cityscapes will yield a merged model within 3.0 mIoU of the ensemble's distilled reference and at least 25 mIoU above naive averaging; kill the idea if the aligned merge remains more than 10 mIoU below the weaker parent, meaning dense architectures block re-basin merging.
why_important: Extends collaborative model construction (merge instead of retrain) to dense perception, relevant wherever data cannot be pooled; also probes whether the linear-mode-connectivity picture survives architectural complexity.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Re-basin alignment is established for classifiers (git-re-basin lineage); the skip-consistent extension to segmentation encoders-decoders with a barrier kill test appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train two DeepLabv3+ models from different seeds on Cityscapes, align with activation-matching under skip constraints, sweep interpolation, and compare barrier heights against classifiers of matched scale.
main_risk: Atrous pyramids and low-level skip fusion may create alignment ambiguities that activation matching cannot resolve, leaving high barriers for reasons unrelated to the core hypothesis.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Independently trained dense models are assumed unmergeable, with ensembling or distillation seen as the only combination routes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Even for classifiers, barrier-free merging often needs width surplus; segmentation models at practical widths may sit in a regime where alignment helps but merging stays useless.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two DeepLabv3+ trainings on Cityscapes (MMSegmentation) plus alignment and interpolation sweeps take about 2 days on one A100; all public.

one_line_idea: Vocabulary-union merging: two detectors finetuned from one base on disjoint category sets merge into a single model detecting the union within a small gap of joint training, eliminating the need to pool datasets for vocabulary growth.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Extending a detector's vocabulary currently requires joint training on combined datasets, which is blocked when datasets cannot be co-located or re-trained at will.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Category knowledge added by finetuning is largely additive in weight space when categories are disjoint (their classifier and mask/box heads occupy separate output slots and their backbone deltas are small and compatible), so merging two disjoint-vocabulary finetunes approximates joint training, with degradation concentrated in categories that are visually confusable across the two sets.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Splitting COCO's 80 classes into two disjoint 40-class finetunes from a shared base and merging, union-evaluation AP will come within 3.0 points of the jointly trained reference, and per-class degradation will correlate with cross-set visual confusability (feature-space class distance) at Spearman rho at least 0.5; kill the idea if the union gap exceeds 8 AP, meaning vocabulary knowledge is not weight-additive.
why_important: Merge-based vocabulary growth is a deployment capability for federated and licensing-constrained settings, and the confusability correlation gives it a predictive theory of when it fails.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Open-vocabulary and incremental detection exist as training paradigms; weight-space vocabulary union with a confusability-based failure model appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Create the disjoint splits, finetune both halves from one Faster R-CNN base, merge with task arithmetic plus output-slot concatenation, and evaluate union AP against joint training with the confusability regression.
main_risk: Background-class semantics differ between the halves (each treats the other's categories as background), injecting a systematic conflict the merge cannot resolve without a data pass.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Vocabulary extension is assumed to require data-level joint training or distillation, not weight-level composition.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The background-conflict mechanism may dominate everything, making merged models hallucinate or suppress across sets and burying the additive structure.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three Faster R-CNN trainings on COCO 40-class splits (MMDetection, 1x) plus merges take about 3 single-A100 days; COCO and base checkpoints public.

one_line_idea: A merge-compatibility rule for the dense-model zoo: mergeability is gated by assignment-mechanism identity (Hungarian-matching vs dense-assignment decoders), a checkable property that predicts merge success better than architecture names or task labels.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Practitioners cannot tell in advance whether two checkpoints will merge productively, and merge attempts are evaluated by trial and error without a governing compatibility principle.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The binding compatibility constraint for dense-model merging is the output-assignment mechanism: models whose training losses assign predictions to targets the same way (both Hungarian set-matching or both dense per-location) shape decoder weight geometry similarly, so assignment identity separates mergeable from unmergeable pairs across backbones and tasks.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across 12 merge pairs constructed to cross assignment mechanism, backbone family, and task, assignment-identity will classify merge success (defined as merged model within 5 points of weaker parent) with at least 80% accuracy, beating task-identity and backbone-identity rules by at least 20 accuracy points; kill the idea if assignment-identity classifies under 60% or fails to beat the alternative rules.
why_important: A checkable compatibility rule converts zoo-wide merging from folklore into a planning tool, and identifies which architectural conventions matter for weight-space composability.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Merge studies rarely vary decoder assignment mechanisms systematically; the assignment-identity rule as the primary compatibility predictor appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble 12 finetune pairs from shared bases spanning the three factors, merge each with standard recipes, tabulate success against the three candidate rules, and report classification accuracies with exact binomial CIs.
main_risk: Twelve pairs give weak statistical power; the factorial must be carefully balanced or the rule comparison becomes anecdote.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Merge compatibility is assumed to track task similarity and shared initialization, with decoder internals treated as irrelevant detail.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Compatibility may be dominated by finetuning distance from the shared base, an axis orthogonal to all three tested rules.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Reusing public finetuned checkpoints where possible and training the remainder (about 8 short finetunes on COCO/ADE20K subsets with MMDetection/MMSegmentation) takes roughly 5 days on one A100; all public.

one_line_idea: Containment-projected part-whole decoding: enforcing part-inside-whole as a hard projection layer at decoding time eliminates containment violations and improves part segmentation without hurting whole-object quality.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Part segmentation models routinely emit parts leaking outside their parent objects, and pipelines either ignore the violations or patch them with ad-hoc post-processing that costs accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part-whole containment is a hard structural prior that current soft losses only approximate; implementing it as a differentiable projection (part logits masked through parent probability) during both training and inference removes an entire error family while acting as a regularizer that sharpens part boundaries against their parent's evidence.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On PartImageNet and PACO, projection decoding will reduce containment-violation pixels to under 5% of their baseline level and improve part mIoU by at least 2.0 points with whole-object mIoU within 0.5 of baseline; kill the idea if part mIoU gains are under 0.5 (projection only cosmetic) or whole-object quality drops by over 1.0.
why_important: Structured outputs with guarantees matter for robotics and editing consumers of part maps, and a projection layer is a reusable component for every hierarchical labeling task.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Hierarchical losses exist for part segmentation; a hard differentiable projection with guarantee-level violation elimination and a part-quality kill line appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train matched part-segmentation models (soft hierarchical loss vs projection decoding) on PartImageNet/PACO, measure violation rates, part mIoU, and whole mIoU, and ablate training-time vs inference-only projection.
main_risk: Hard projection couples part errors to parent errors: where the parent mask is wrong, parts cannot recover, potentially concentrating failures on hard images.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Structural consistency is treated as a soft-loss preference or a post-processing detail rather than an architectural guarantee.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Violations may already be rare enough on modern models that eliminating them moves no headline metric, making the guarantee practically weightless.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two Mask2Former-based part trainings on PartImageNet take about 1.5 days on one A100; PartImageNet, PACO, and baselines are public.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: hard containment projection vs soft hierarchical loss

one_line_idea: Relational-consistency re-decoding for detection: an energy-based pass that rescoring detections against learned object-relation statistics (support, co-occurrence, relative scale) recovers context-inconsistent misses and suppresses relation-violating false positives.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detectors score each object nearly independently, and relation-level nonsense (a rider without any ridden vehicle overlapping, a monitor floating without support) survives to the output because nothing in decoding checks it.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Scene-level relational statistics learned from annotation graphs constitute an output-space prior that detection decoding can consume: joint rescoring under a relational energy fixes errors invisible to per-object confidence, and the fix concentrates on relation-implicated classes where local evidence is genuinely ambiguous.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Visual Genome-annotated COCO imagery, relational re-decoding of a frozen public detector will improve AP on relation-implicated classes by at least 1.5 points at unchanged overall AP (within 0.3), with at least 60% of corrected instances involving the modeled relations; kill the idea if relation-implicated gains are under 0.5 AP, meaning per-object confidence already absorbs contextual evidence.
why_important: Adds a modular structural-reasoning capability on top of any frozen detector, and quantifies how much detection error is relational rather than appearance-based.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Context rescoring is classical (pre-deep detection era); a modern energy-based re-decoding over frozen detector outputs with relation-attributed accounting appears fresh.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit relational statistics from Visual Genome, implement joint rescoring over top-k detections of a public Faster R-CNN/DINO-DETR, and evaluate class-stratified AP with attribution of corrections to specific relations.
main_risk: Modern detectors' backbones may already encode context implicitly, leaving relational re-decoding to correct only rare tail cases at the cost of new relation-induced errors.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Context modeling is considered obsolete since deep backbones absorbed it into features.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Relation statistics from noisy annotation graphs may be too biased toward photographed-scene conventions, hurting exactly the unusual scenes where corrections would matter.

one_line_idea: Connectivity-constrained lane decoding: decoding lane markings as connected curve sets with a hard continuity constraint halves broken-lane errors at equal pixel accuracy, because breakage is an output-space artifact rather than a perception failure.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Per-pixel lane segmentation produces fragmented lanes under occlusion and wear, and downstream planners consume connectivity, not pixels, so fragmentation is the operative failure mode.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most lane breaks occur where per-pixel evidence dips below threshold while curve-level evidence remains strong, so decoding into an explicit curve space (ordered point sequences with continuity constraints) converts marginal pixel evidence into connected outputs, cutting breakage without new supervision.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On BDD100K lane annotations, constrained curve decoding of the same backbone will reduce broken-lane rate (ground-truth lanes split into 2+ predicted fragments) by at least 50% relative at matched pixel-F1 (within 1.0), and gains will concentrate on occluded/worn segments; kill the idea if breakage reduction is under 15% at matched F1, meaning breaks reflect missing evidence, not decoding.
why_important: Aligns the output space with what consumers of lane maps actually need, and cleanly separates perception failure from representation failure with a matched-accuracy design.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Curve-based lane methods exist; the matched-pixel-accuracy breakage attribution (decoding vs evidence) with a kill line appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train pixel and curve-decoding heads on one frozen backbone on BDD100K lanes, match pixel-F1 by operating point, and compare breakage statistics stratified by occlusion/wear tags.
main_risk: Hard continuity can hallucinate lanes across genuine gaps (intersections, merges), introducing planner-dangerous false continuity that the breakage metric does not penalize.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Lane fragmentation is treated as an evidence problem to fix with better features or more data rather than an output-space problem.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If breaks co-locate with truly ambiguous road segments, constrained decoding will trade breakage for hallucination one-for-one, failing the safety-relevant tradeoff.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two head trainings on frozen DINOv2 features over BDD100K (public) take under 1 day on one consumer GPU; dataset and backbones public.

one_line_idea: Hierarchy-consistent decoding for classification: constraining predictions to respect the WordNet hierarchy at decode time reduces severe mistakes substantially at equal top-1, delivering the mistake-severity benefit of hierarchical training without retraining.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Flat classifiers make severe mistakes (dog to dishwasher) that hierarchy-aware training reduces, but retraining the deployed zoo with hierarchical objectives is impractical.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Much of the severe-mistake problem is a decoding artifact: flat argmax discards the hierarchical structure already implicit in logit correlations, so a decode-time procedure that aggregates evidence up the WordNet tree and selects the deepest sufficiently supported node cuts mistake severity on existing frozen checkpoints.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On ImageNet-1k with 10 public classifiers, tree-aggregated decoding will reduce mean hierarchical mistake severity (tree distance of errors) by at least 15% at top-1 within 0.3 of baseline, and will beat logit-smoothing controls by at least 8% severity reduction; kill the idea if severity improvement at matched top-1 is under 5%, meaning the structure is not recoverable from frozen logits.
why_important: Severity-aware outputs matter in deployment (a wrong-species label is tolerable, a wrong-kingdom label is not), and a decode-only method upgrades every existing checkpoint for free.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Hierarchy-aware training (making-better-mistakes lineage) is established; matched-top-1 decode-time recovery of that benefit on frozen models appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement tree-evidence aggregation over frozen logits of 10 timm checkpoints, tune the support threshold for matched top-1, and compare severity distributions against argmax and smoothing controls.
main_risk: Logit correlations may encode co-occurrence rather than taxonomy, causing tree aggregation to help on some branches and hurt on others with no net gain.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Mistake severity is assumed to require training-time hierarchical objectives; decoding is treated as argmax by definition.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If flat training linearizes away hierarchical structure in the logit space, no decode-time procedure can recover distinctions the network never preserved.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference-cached logits for 10 public timm models on ImageNet val plus decoding sweeps run in under 4 hours on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Correction propagation across a dataset: one human fix to a model error, matched through frozen-feature similarity, automatically repairs the same error mode across thousands of images with bounded collateral damage.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Model errors on a dataset cluster into repeated modes (same class confusion, same boundary bias), yet human corrections in review tools fix one instance at a time and discard the information the correction carries about the mode.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Error modes are compact neighborhoods in frozen self-supervised feature space, so a single correction defines a search template whose nearest-neighbor matches (with a conservative acceptance threshold) are overwhelmingly instances of the same mistake, enabling one-to-many correction with a measurable precision-collateral tradeoff.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On ADE20K predictions from a public model, propagating single corrections through DINOv2-feature matching will fix at least 30% of same-mode errors (mode defined by a held-out human audit) at under 5% collateral damage (correct predictions wrongly altered); kill the idea if fixing under 10% of the mode at 5% collateral, meaning error modes are not feature-compact.
why_important: Multiplies the value of every human review action by orders of magnitude, converting dataset QA and model-output review from linear to sublinear cost in error count.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Similarity search and error clustering exist separately; a corrected-instance-as-query propagation protocol with an audited precision-collateral frontier appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run a public segmentation model over ADE20K val, have an auditor label error modes on a sample, simulate single corrections per mode, propagate via feature matching at swept thresholds, and measure mode-fix rate versus collateral.
main_risk: Some error modes are context-driven rather than appearance-driven (errors under particular scene layouts), which appearance-feature matching will miss entirely.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Corrections are treated as per-instance data points for eventual retraining, not as immediately actionable dataset-wide operations.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Feature neighborhoods may mix correct and incorrect instances of similar appearance so tightly that no threshold achieves useful fix rates at acceptable collateral.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference plus DINOv2 feature indexing over ADE20K and propagation sweeps run in under 8 hours on one consumer GPU, plus roughly 4 hours of human error-mode auditing; all data and models public.

one_line_idea: Learned click policies for interactive segmentation: a policy trained to choose the next click location (rather than the fixed largest-error-center heuristic) reduces clicks-to-target-quality by a quarter across datasets and models.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Interactive segmentation training and evaluation hard-code the next-click rule (center of the largest error region), a heuristic never validated as an efficient interaction policy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Click value is a learnable function of the current prediction state (uncertainty structure, boundary geometry, error topology), so a policy trained with lookahead simulation places clicks where expected quality gain is maximal, dominating the fixed heuristic especially in the low-click regime where placement matters most.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On standard interactive benchmarks (GrabCut, Berkeley, SBD, DAVIS-static frames) with a public interactive model, the learned policy will reduce mean clicks to 90% IoU by at least 25% relative to the largest-error-center heuristic, and transfer across model checkpoints losing under half its advantage; kill the idea if click savings are under 10% on the majority of benchmarks, meaning the heuristic is near-optimal.
why_important: Interaction budgets are the real currency of annotation tooling; a validated policy improves every deployed interactive labeler without touching the segmentation model.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Interactive models improved rapidly while the interaction policy stayed fixed; policy learning over click placement with cross-model transfer tests appears under-explored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train a click-policy network via simulated rollouts on COCO instances using a frozen public interactive model, then evaluate clicks-to-quality on held-out benchmarks against heuristic and random policies with both the training model and an unseen model.
main_risk: The policy may overfit the specific error patterns of its training model, and the cross-model transfer test could reveal it learned model quirks rather than interaction principles.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The largest-error-center rule is assumed close enough to optimal that policy learning is not worth the complexity.
why_it_might_be_wrong: In the low-click regime, most instances may be solved by any sensible click, compressing the room between heuristic and optimal to a few percent.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Policy training with a frozen public SimpleClick/RITM checkpoint plus GrabCut/Berkeley/SBD benchmark evaluations runs in about 1.5 days on one consumer GPU; all datasets and models public.

one_line_idea: Exclusion prompts as a first-class interaction type: adding not-this clicks that carve away distractor regions cuts interaction budgets on cluttered scenes beyond what additional positive clicks achieve.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Interactive segmentation interfaces offer positive and background clicks, but background clicks are weak in cluttered scenes where the failure is confusion with a specific adjacent distractor object rather than generic background.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Distractor confusion is object-level, not pixel-level: an exclusion prompt bound to the distractor's full extent (via a class-agnostic proposal under the click) removes the entire confusable region in one action, so exclusion clicks dominate background clicks in per-click information on cluttered scenes.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On high-clutter subsets of SBD and COCO instances, models retrained with exclusion-prompt channels will reduce clicks to 90% IoU by at least 25% versus positive+background prompting, while low-clutter performance changes by under 5%; kill the idea if cluttered-scene click savings are under 8%, meaning object-level exclusion adds nothing over pixel-level background clicks.
why_important: Expands the interaction vocabulary of every annotation and editing tool with a measurable efficiency win precisely on the scenes where current tools are slowest.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Positive/negative click training is standard; object-extent-bound exclusion semantics with a clutter-stratified evaluation appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Extend a public interactive model with an exclusion channel that consumes proposal masks under negative clicks, retrain with simulated interactions on COCO, and evaluate clutter-stratified clicks-to-quality against the standard prompt vocabulary.
main_risk: Exclusion semantics depend on proposal quality under the click; bad proposals could make exclusion clicks destructive and user-hostile.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Background clicks are assumed to already express everything a negative interaction needs to say.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern models may resolve distractor confusion with one well-placed positive click anyway, leaving exclusion prompts redundant in practice.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Retraining SimpleClick-style models with the extra channel on COCO subsets takes about 1 day on one consumer GPU; SBD, COCO, and baseline checkpoints public.

one_line_idea: Batch prompting through correspondence: one prompted image labels a hundred similar images by transporting the prompt through dense correspondences, achieving most of per-image prompting quality at a fraction of the interaction cost.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Prompt-based mask engines (the SAM family among them) require prompting every image separately even when a batch of images shares content structure, as in product photography, repeated inspection views, or media archives of the same scene type.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For visually coherent batches, prompts are transportable: dense semantic correspondence from the prompted image to each batch member relocates the prompt with enough precision that the mask engine's output quality approaches native per-image prompting, making interaction cost sublinear in batch size.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On batches assembled from ImageNet class folders and PASCAL categories, correspondence-transported prompts will reach at least 80% of per-image-prompting mask IoU on 100-image batches from a single prompted exemplar, versus under 55% for center-prior transport baselines; kill the idea if transported quality falls under 60% of native prompting, meaning correspondence precision is insufficient for prompt reuse.
why_important: Makes prompt-based segmentation economical at archive scale, converting per-image interaction into per-batch interaction for the large fraction of real workloads with internal visual coherence.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Dense correspondence and promptable segmentation are established separately; prompt transport as a batch-labeling protocol with quality-retention accounting appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build coherent batches, compute DINOv2-feature correspondences from the exemplar, transport point/box prompts to each member, run the public SAM checkpoint on transported prompts, and compare against native prompting and transport baselines.
main_risk: Batch coherence in the wild is weaker than in class folders, and the protocol's value depends on a coherence-detection front end this experiment does not build.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Prompting is assumed inherently per-image, with batch efficiency pursued through model finetuning rather than prompt reuse.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Correspondence fails exactly on deformable or rotated instances where prompting precision matters, potentially capping transported quality below usefulness.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Correspondence computation plus mask-engine inference (public SAM ViT-B checkpoint, DINOv2 features) over 2k images runs in under 6 hours on one consumer GPU; ImageNet/PASCAL data public.

one_line_idea: Optimal single-question disambiguation: when a prompt is ambiguous between part, object, and group, one automatically chosen binary question (is the handle included?) resolves the ambiguity more reliably than an extra click, measured by post-interaction accuracy.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Point prompts are systematically ambiguous across granularity levels (part vs whole vs group), and mask engines answer with multi-mask outputs that push the choice back onto the user interface without structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Granularity ambiguity is low-dimensional and query-resolvable: the candidate masks' symmetric differences identify a maximally informative region, and a single yes/no question about that region (rendered visually) collapses the hypothesis set more reliably than an additional click, because clicks are themselves granularity-ambiguous.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On granularity-ambiguous prompts sampled from PACO and PartImageNet instances (part/whole annotations available), the one-question protocol will select the user-intended granularity at least 85% of the time versus at most 65% for one extra click, at equal interaction count; kill the idea if question-based resolution is within 5 points of click-based, meaning questions carry no advantage over spatial interaction.
why_important: Defines a principled disambiguation turn for every prompt-based tool, replacing ad-hoc multi-mask pickers with an interaction whose information value is measurable and optimizable.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Multi-mask ambiguity outputs exist in public mask engines; treating disambiguation as optimal binary questioning over mask hypotheses with a click-controlled comparison appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample ambiguous prompts on part-annotated instances, simulate user intents from the annotation hierarchy, implement difference-region questioning versus extra-click baselines, and compare intent-match rates at fixed interaction budgets.
main_risk: Simulated intent distributions may not match real user intent frequencies, and the advantage could invert if real users mostly want whole objects.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Ambiguity handling is treated as a UI concern (show three masks) rather than an optimizable interaction-design problem.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Rendering and answering a visual question may cost more user time than a click, so equal-interaction-count comparisons may hide a worse time-per-decision tradeoff.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Simulation-based evaluation over PACO/PartImageNet with a public promptable mask engine (the SAM ViT-B checkpoint) runs in under 6 hours on one consumer GPU; all data and checkpoints public.

one_line_idea: Prompt-once, read-many consistency: a shared prompt encoder that drives segmentation, part, and attribute heads from one prompt produces mutually consistent multi-task outputs, halving cross-head contradiction rates at equal per-task accuracy.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Pipelines that need multiple outputs about one prompted object (mask, parts, attributes) run separate models whose outputs contradict each other (attributes of a different instance, parts leaking outside the mask), and contradictions are handled by glue code.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-head contradictions stem from independent instance grounding: sharing a single prompt-conditioned object embedding across heads forces all outputs to describe the same grounded instance, cutting contradictions structurally rather than by post-hoc filtering.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On PACO (masks, parts, attributes available), the shared-embedding multi-head model will cut cross-output contradiction rates (attribute-mask disagreement, part-outside-mask pixels) by at least 50% relative to independently grounded heads at per-task metrics within 1.0 point; kill the idea if contradiction reduction is under 15% or any task loses over 2.0 points, meaning shared grounding taxes accuracy more than it buys coherence.
why_important: Output coherence is the operative quality for editing and robotics consumers who act on multiple predictions jointly; making it structural is a reusable design capability.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Multi-task heads and promptable engines exist; contradiction rate as a first-class optimized metric with shared-grounding architecture appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train shared-embedding and independent-head variants on PACO from the same frozen backbone, define contradiction metrics over paired outputs, and compare coherence and per-task quality.
main_risk: Contradiction metrics must be carefully defined to avoid rewarding degenerate coupling (e.g., attribute head copying mask confidence), requiring adversarial metric review.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Output consistency is assumed to be a downstream integration problem, not an architectural objective worth trading capacity for.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Contradictions may mostly arise on instances where all heads are wrong anyway, so structural coupling reduces measured contradictions without improving usable output quality.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two head-set trainings on PACO over frozen DINOv2 features take about 1 day on one consumer GPU; PACO and backbones public.

one_line_idea: Interaction-noise training for prompt robustness: injecting realistic misclick and imprecision noise into prompt simulation during training halves output variance under real-user-level prompt jitter without degrading clean-prompt accuracy.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Interactive and promptable models are trained with idealized simulated prompts (exact centers, clean boundary clicks), while real users misclick by many pixels, and model outputs can change discontinuously under such jitter.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompt sensitivity is an artifact of the clean-prompt training distribution rather than an inherent property: training with an empirically calibrated interaction-noise model (spatial jitter, wrong-instance clicks at plausible rates) smooths the prompt-to-output map, reducing jitter variance at no cost to clean performance because the noise model covers rather than replaces the clean cases.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Under test-time prompt jitter matching a plausible user model (10-pixel sigma), noise-trained interactive models will show at least 50% lower output IoU variance and at least 3.0 points higher worst-case IoU than clean-trained twins, with clean-prompt IoU within 0.5; kill the idea if jitter-variance reduction is under 20% or clean performance drops over 1.0, meaning robustness and precision genuinely trade off.
why_important: Robustness to interaction noise is the difference between demo quality and product quality for every promptable perception tool, and the fix is a training-data policy, not an architecture.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Prompt simulation is standard; empirically calibrated interaction-noise training with variance-based robustness accounting appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Calibrate a noise model from published human-clicking statistics or a small collection, retrain a public interactive architecture with and without noise injection on COCO, and evaluate jitter-variance and worst-case metrics on SBD/GrabCut.
main_risk: If no public human-clicking statistics suffice, calibrating the noise model requires a small user study, adding a human-subjects dependency to an otherwise scripted experiment.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Prompt precision is treated as the user's responsibility, and training-time interaction noise is assumed to blur model competence.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Discontinuous output changes under jitter may reflect genuine scene ambiguity boundaries that no training distribution can smooth without losing expressiveness.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two interactive-model trainings (SimpleClick-style on COCO subsets) plus jitter evaluations take about 1 day on one consumer GPU; all data and baselines public.

one_line_idea: Object-adversarial attribute factorization: training the attribute pathway with gradient reversal against object identity yields attribute features that recombine with unseen objects, lifting unseen-composition recognition beyond joint-head baselines.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Compositional zero-shot recognition (unseen attribute-object pairs like wet dog after training on wet cat and dry dog) remains far below seen-pair accuracy, with attribute representations entangled with the objects they were observed on.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The entanglement is a removable training artifact: an explicit adversarial term that strips object-identity information from the attribute pathway (gradient reversal on an object probe) forces attribute features to encode transferable appearance transformations, and recombination accuracy rises in proportion to how much object information is removed.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On MIT-States and UT-Zappos, the object-adversarial factorized model will improve unseen-pair accuracy by at least 3.0 points over the same architecture without the adversarial term, and the improvement will correlate across runs with the object-probe accuracy drop in the attribute pathway (rho at least 0.5); kill the idea if unseen-pair gains are under 1.0 point or uncorrelated with measured disentanglement, breaking the mechanism.
why_important: Compositional generalization is the difference between recognizing a catalog and understanding visual structure; a mechanism-verified factorization method moves the field beyond loss-cocktail engineering.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Compositional zero-shot learning has many factorization attempts; tying the claim to a measured disentanglement-to-generalization correlation with a kill line appears uncommon.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train matched models with and without gradient reversal on standard CZSL splits, measure unseen-pair accuracy and attribute-pathway object-probe accuracy across 5 seeds, and run the correlation analysis.
main_risk: Some attributes are object-conditional by nature (ripe means different things for banana and tomato), and aggressive de-objectification could destroy exactly those attributes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Compositional failure is often attributed to dataset scale and label noise rather than to a fixable entanglement mechanism in the representation.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Gradient-reversal probes remove linearly accessible information only; the entanglement may be nonlinear and survive, leaving gains within noise.
fastest_falsification_experiment: CZSL trainings on MIT-States/UT-Zappos with a frozen public backbone (DINOv2 or OpenCLIP features) take under 1 day for all arms on one consumer GPU; datasets and backbones public.

one_line_idea: Translational relation composition: embedding visual relations as vector translations between subject and object features enables zero-shot recognition of unseen subject-relation-object triplets at rates well above joint-classifier baselines.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Visual relationship detection degrades sharply on triplets absent from training, because standard heads memorize triplet statistics rather than composing relation meaning with participants.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Many visual relations act approximately as consistent transformations in a well-shaped feature space (the knowledge-graph translation intuition transported to vision), so constraining relation embeddings to operate translationally between subject and object features yields compositional generalization that joint softmax heads structurally cannot achieve.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Visual Genome zero-shot triplet splits, the translational head will improve zero-shot triplet recall@50 by at least 30% relative over a parameter-matched joint classifier on the same frozen detector features, while seen-triplet recall stays within 5% relative; kill the idea if zero-shot improvement is under 10% relative, meaning translational structure does not fit visual relations.
why_important: Establishes whether relational composition in vision is representable by simple algebra, a foundational question with direct payoff for open-world scene understanding.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Translation embeddings are classical in knowledge graphs and appeared in early VRD works; a modern frozen-VFM-feature instantiation with matched-parameter controls and relative kill thresholds appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Extract subject/object features from a frozen public detector on Visual Genome, train translational and joint heads at matched parameters, and evaluate seen/zero-shot triplet recall.
main_risk: Spatially mediated relations (above, under) may fit translation while interaction relations (riding, eating) do not, yielding a mixed verdict that weakens the headline claim.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Zero-shot triplet failure is treated as a data coverage problem to be solved by scale rather than by output-space algebra.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Feature spaces optimized for detection may lack the metric regularity translation requires, making the constraint a handicap instead of an inductive bias.

one_line_idea: Region-tokenized pooling preserves feature binding: replacing global pooling with segmentation-guided region tokens fixes the two-object attribute-binding failures of pooled representations, on natural images and without language supervision.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Pooled image representations fail binding tests (red cube next to blue sphere is indistinguishable from blue cube next to red sphere), a failure documented mostly on language-supervised models but structurally present in any global pooling.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Binding failure is a pooling artifact, not a representation deficit: the spatial feature map retains per-object attribute information that global pooling destroys, so a region-tokenized readout (pool within class-agnostic segments, classify per token, aggregate relationally) restores binding without retraining the backbone.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On two-object binding probes built from CLEVR and from natural COCO two-instance images, region-token readout of a frozen backbone will answer attribute-binding queries at over 80% accuracy where global-pooling readout scores under 60%, with the gap surviving on the natural-image probe; kill the idea if region tokens fail to beat pooling by at least 10 points on natural images, meaning binding information dies before the pooling stage.
why_important: Locates the binding bottleneck precisely (readout vs representation) and ships the repair as a readout module compatible with every frozen backbone.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Binding critiques exist for CLIP-style models; a stage-attribution experiment with a region-token repair validated on natural images appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct binding probes (synthetic CLEVR pairs, natural COCO pairs with distinct-color same-category instances), compare global-pool vs region-token readout of frozen DINOv2/OpenCLIP with matched probe capacity, and attribute failures by stage.
main_risk: Natural-image binding probes must control low-level shortcuts (color-position correlations), or the region-token advantage could reflect probe construction rather than binding.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Binding failure is discussed as a representational limitation of contrastive pretraining rather than as a readout-stage artifact.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Attribute information may be genuinely delocalized in deep layers (mixed by attention), in which case even region pooling cannot rebind it and the repair fails.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Probe construction and readout comparisons over frozen public backbones (DINOv2, OpenCLIP) run in under 6 hours on one consumer GPU; CLEVR, COCO, and all checkpoints public.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: region-tokenized vs global pooling of frozen features

one_line_idea: Part-graph recognition for viewpoint compositionality: classifying objects through an explicit part-and-adjacency graph retains accuracy on held-out viewpoints where holistic classifiers collapse, quantifying the structural route to pose generalization.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Classifiers degrade on object viewpoints unseen in training, and the standard remedy is more viewpoint data rather than representations that generalize structurally.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Viewpoint change preserves part identity and adjacency while scrambling holistic appearance, so a recognizer operating on a detected part graph (parts as nodes, adjacency as edges, pose-invariant descriptors) retains far more accuracy on held-out viewpoints than holistic baselines of matched capacity, isolating composition as the generalization mechanism.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On PASCAL3D+ with azimuth-held-out splits (train on front/side, test on rear/oblique), the part-graph model will retain at least 75% of its seen-viewpoint accuracy versus under 55% retention for the holistic baseline, and ablating adjacency structure will remove at least half the retention advantage; kill the idea if retention advantage is under 5 points, meaning part structure adds nothing beyond features.
why_important: Provides causal evidence for or against the long-claimed compositional route to viewpoint robustness, with an architecture usable wherever pose diversity in training data is unattainable.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Part-based models are classical; a controlled viewpoint-held-out retention comparison against matched holistic baselines on modern features appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Detect parts with a public part segmenter on PASCAL3D+ categories, train graph and holistic classifiers at matched parameters on restricted-azimuth splits, and compare retention with the adjacency ablation.
main_risk: Part detection itself may fail on held-out viewpoints, entangling the part-detector's generalization with the graph classifier's and muddying attribution.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Viewpoint robustness is assumed to come from data diversity and augmentation, with explicit part structure regarded as an obsolete inductive bias.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern SSL features may already be viewpoint-tolerant enough that holistic retention matches structural retention, closing the gap the hypothesis needs.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Part extraction plus classifier trainings on PASCAL3D+ (public) with frozen DINOv2 features take under 1 day on one consumer GPU; all public. Scope note: this tests 2D recognition robustness across viewpoints, not 3D reconstruction or geometry estimation.

one_line_idea: Exemplar-difference queries: specifying a visual concept by positive minus negative exemplar sets (cups, minus cups-with-handles) defines a retrieval and detection interface that resolves concepts names cannot express, with measurable precision on public data.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Many practically needed visual concepts are name-resistant (a specific damage pattern, a style variant, an absence like missing-cap), and text-grounded interfaces force users to approximate them with clumsy phrases.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Frozen feature spaces support subtractive concept specification: the direction defined by contrasting positive and negative exemplar means (with whitening against nuisance variation) isolates the differentiating property, enabling retrieval and detection of the differential concept at precision far above nearest-neighbor-to-positives baselines.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On differential-concept tasks constructed from PACO attribute annotations (object-with-attribute minus object-without), exemplar-difference queries with 5+5 exemplars will achieve at least 2x the retrieval precision@50 of positive-only nearest-neighbor baselines and at least 80% of a supervised linear probe trained on 100 labels; kill the idea if the difference query beats positives-only by under 20% relative, meaning subtraction adds nothing in these feature spaces.
why_important: Defines a practical no-training concept interface for the long tail of unnameable visual needs, and measures how algebraically usable frozen feature geometry actually is.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Concept directions via embedding arithmetic are folklore for word vectors and GAN latents; a benchmarked exemplar-difference protocol for frozen perception features with supervised-probe reference points appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build differential tasks from PACO attribute pairs, implement whitened difference queries over DINOv2/OpenCLIP features, and evaluate retrieval precision against positives-only, random-negative, and supervised-probe references.
main_risk: Nuisance whitening requires estimating covariance from few exemplars, and poor estimates may make results exemplar-set-luck-dominated, demanding many resamples.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Concept specification is assumed to route through language or finetuning, with embedding arithmetic dismissed as unreliable outside toy demos.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Attribute differences may not be linearly separable from object identity in frozen spaces, collapsing difference directions into noise for exactly the subtle concepts that motivate the interface.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feature extraction and retrieval sweeps over PACO with public DINOv2 and OpenCLIP backbones run in under 4 hours on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Context-swap training for context-robust recognition: replacing backgrounds with segmentation-guided plausible alternatives during training yields classifiers that keep in-context accuracy while gaining strongly on out-of-context objects.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Classifiers lean on background context, and accuracy collapses for objects photographed outside habitual contexts, a failure documented by out-of-context test sets but usually addressed only by evaluation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Context reliance is a training-distribution artifact that targeted intervention can remove without sacrificing the legitimate uses of context: swapping backgrounds for a controlled fraction of training images (using instance masks and diverse-scene targets) breaks the spurious object-context coupling while preserving object evidence, so out-of-context accuracy rises with minimal in-context cost.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Training on COCO-derived classification with 30% context-swapped images will improve out-of-context accuracy (objects composited into unusual scenes, plus natural out-of-context test images) by at least 8.0 points while in-context accuracy stays within 1.5; kill the idea if out-of-context gains are under 3.0 points or in-context cost exceeds 3.0, meaning context reliance is not separable by this intervention.
why_important: Converts the out-of-context debunk literature into a costed training-policy repair, quantifying the tradeoff frontier between context use and context robustness.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Background-swap augmentation appears in scattered robustness works; a swap-fraction frontier with natural out-of-context validation and pre-registered kill thresholds appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build the swap pipeline from COCO masks and Places-style scene targets, sweep the swap fraction, train matched classifiers, and evaluate on composited and natural out-of-context probes plus standard in-context tests.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts could teach edge cues that inflate composited-probe gains without transferring to natural out-of-context images, which the natural probe is designed to catch.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Context reliance is treated as an inherent statistical property of discriminative training, with out-of-context failure accepted as unavoidable.
why_it_might_be_wrong: For small objects, context may carry most of the legitimate signal, and swapping could cost more in-context accuracy than the frontier tolerates.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Swap-pipeline construction plus four classifier trainings (timm ResNet-50/ViT-S on COCO-crop classification) take about 1.5 days on one A100; COCO, Places365, and models public.

one_line_idea: A frozen class-agnostic boundary stream as a universal instance prior: feeding generic boundary-detector features alongside backbone features improves instance segmentation on datasets never seen by either component, because instance separation is boundary-limited out of domain.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Instance segmentation transfers poorly to unseen datasets, and the dominant failure is merged adjacent instances rather than misclassification, yet transfer recipes focus on class adaptation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Class-agnostic boundary perception is the most transferable component of instance segmentation: a frozen boundary stream trained once on generic edge/boundary data supplies separation evidence that dataset-specific training cannot unlearn, so plugging it into any instance architecture improves out-of-domain instance separation specifically.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Adding the frozen boundary stream to Mask2Former trained on COCO and evaluated zero-shot on Cityscapes and LVIS-rare imagery will improve out-of-domain mask-AP by at least 1.5 points with merged-instance errors reduced by at least 25%, while in-domain COCO change stays within 0.3; kill the idea if out-of-domain gains are under 0.5 AP or do not concentrate on merge errors, breaking the mechanism claim.
why_important: Identifies which sub-skill of instance segmentation transfers and packages it as a reusable module, converting an observed transfer pathology into an architectural capability.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Boundary-aware segmentation exists in-domain; framing a frozen generic boundary stream as a transfer prior with merge-error attribution appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train the boundary stream on BSDS500 plus generic contour data, integrate as a frozen input branch to Mask2Former, train on COCO, and evaluate zero-shot on Cityscapes/LVIS with merge-error decomposition.
main_risk: Boundary detectors themselves degrade out of domain, potentially shifting rather than solving the transfer bottleneck.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Transfer failure in instance segmentation is treated as a class/appearance adaptation problem, with boundary competence assumed to come along for free.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Merged-instance errors may stem from query assignment rather than missing boundary evidence, in which case extra boundary input changes nothing.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Boundary-stream training on BSDS500 (hours) plus two Mask2Former COCO trainings and zero-shot evaluations take about 3 days on one A100; BSDS500, COCO, Cityscapes, LVIS all public.

one_line_idea: Mask-derived box supervision sharpens localization: refitting training boxes from instance masks (which encode extent more precisely than drawn boxes) improves tight-IoU detection metrics with zero new annotation.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detection ground-truth boxes are drawn independently of masks even where masks exist, and drawn boxes carry systematic slack (loose margins, inconsistent extremity handling) that becomes the regression target.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Box-drawing slack is a supervision noise floor for localization: replacing drawn boxes with mask-tight refits where masks exist removes a biased noise component, so models trained on refit boxes improve specifically at strict IoU thresholds (AP75, AP90) where slack dominates the error budget.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Training public detectors on COCO with mask-refit boxes will improve AP75 by at least 1.0 and AP90 by at least 1.5 points at AP50 within 0.3 of baseline, and the improvement will scale with each class's measured drawn-box slack (rho at least 0.5); kill the idea if AP75 gains are under 0.3, meaning drawn-box noise is below the learning noise floor.
why_important: A free supervision upgrade for every masked detection dataset, plus a quantified accounting of how much localization ceiling is annotation slack rather than model limitation.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Mask-to-box conversion is trivial tooling; treating drawn-box slack as a measurable supervision noise source with strict-threshold predictions appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure drawn-vs-refit box deltas on COCO, retrain Faster R-CNN and DINO-DETR on refit boxes, evaluate the AP threshold spectrum, and run the per-class slack-to-gain regression.
main_risk: Evaluation ground truth keeps drawn-box conventions, so refit-trained models could be penalized at test time for being right, requiring dual evaluation against refit and original references.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Ground-truth boxes are treated as definitionally correct targets, with localization improvements sought entirely on the model side.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Mask boundary errors may inject as much noise as box slack removes, netting zero at every threshold.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Box refitting is scripted; two detector retrainings on COCO (MMDetection 1x) take about 2 single-A100 days; all public.

one_line_idea: Part-segmentation auxiliary supervision for occluded keypoints: jointly training 2D pose with human-part masks improves occluded-joint localization specifically, because part extents carry the evidence that point supervision under occlusion lacks.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] 2D pose estimators fail disproportionately on occluded joints, whose point annotations provide no spatial support for learning what partial visibility looks like.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part masks are the natural auxiliary supervision for occlusion: they define the visible support region of each limb, so a shared-feature model trained on keypoints plus part masks learns visibility-conditional evidence integration, improving occluded-joint PCK while leaving visible joints unchanged, with the gain mediated by part-mask quality.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Joint training on COCO keypoints and DensePose/LIP part masks will improve occlusion-flagged-joint PCK by at least 2.0 points with visible-joint PCK within 0.3, beating a multi-task control trained with an unrelated auxiliary task (segmentation of non-person classes) by at least 1.2 points on occluded joints; kill the idea if occluded-joint gains are under 0.7 or the unrelated-task control matches the part-mask auxiliary, meaning the gain is generic multi-task regularization.
why_important: Targets the acknowledged weak point of 2D pose with a mechanism-specific auxiliary and an unusually clean control that separates task synergy from regularization.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pose-and-parsing multi-task models exist; the occlusion-stratified analysis with an unrelated-auxiliary control isolating the mechanism appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train ViTPose-style models with keypoint-only, keypoint+part-mask, and keypoint+unrelated-auxiliary objectives on COCO/LIP, and compare occlusion-stratified PCK.
main_risk: Part-mask datasets differ in imagery and pose distribution from the keypoint dataset, so multi-dataset multi-task training may introduce confounds the control cannot fully absorb.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Occluded-joint failure is treated as a data-volume issue for pose alone, with part parsing regarded as a separate application rather than a supervision source.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Heatmap models may already infer visible support implicitly, leaving part masks redundant with what pose supervision teaches.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three pose trainings on COCO keypoints with LIP auxiliary data (public ViTPose recipes) take about 3 days total on one A100; all datasets and baselines public.

one_line_idea: Self-supervised attention as an open-world objectness prior: injecting SSL attention-derived objectness into proposal generation recovers novel-class proposals that supervised RPNs suppress, raising open-set recall without hurting known classes.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Supervised proposal networks learn the annotated vocabulary's notion of objectness and systematically miss unannotated novel objects, capping every open-world pipeline at the proposal stage.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Self-supervised attention maps encode a vocabulary-free objectness signal (SSL training never saw class labels), so fusing an SSL-attention objectness channel into proposal scoring recovers novel-object proposals that supervised objectness suppresses, with the improvement concentrated on classes absent from detection training.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO-trained detectors evaluated for proposal recall on LVIS classes disjoint from COCO, SSL-attention fusion will improve novel-class average recall (AR@100) by at least 5.0 points with COCO-class AR within 1.0, and a supervised-attention placebo (attention from a supervised classifier) will capture under half the gain; kill the idea if novel-class AR improves by under 1.5 points or the placebo matches SSL fusion, meaning the effect is generic attention, not label-free objectness.
why_important: Repairs the proposal bottleneck of open-world detection with a frozen, label-free component and pins the mechanism (vocabulary-free training) with a placebo control.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] SSL attention localization is documented (DINO-attention lineage); its fusion into proposal scoring with a supervised-attention placebo and novel-class kill thresholds appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fuse DINOv2 attention objectness into RPN scoring of a COCO-trained Faster R-CNN, evaluate proposal recall on LVIS-only classes, and run the supervised-attention placebo arm.
main_risk: SSL attention emphasizes salient central objects and may miss exactly the small peripheral novel objects open-world use cases care about.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Proposal networks are assumed to generalize objectness beyond their training vocabulary well enough that the proposal stage is not the open-world bottleneck.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Novel-class misses may occur at the classification stage rather than proposal stage in modern architectures, making proposal-level repair moot.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference-plus-refit experiments with public Faster R-CNN, DINOv2, and a supervised ViT on COCO/LVIS take under 1 day on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Stuff-context conditioning for thing detection: conditioning detector queries on stuff-segmentation tokens improves context-dependent object classes, quantifying how much detection has been leaving on the table by ignoring stuff.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detection architectures consume backbone features but no explicit scene-stuff representation, even though many object classes (parking meter, traffic light, buoy) are defined largely by the stuff context they stand in.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Explicit stuff tokens (pooled per stuff region from a segmentation head) provide a structured context signal that raw features do not surface at detection-decoder granularity, so query conditioning on stuff tokens improves context-dependent classes specifically, with gains proportional to each class's measured stuff-context mutual information.

why_important: Tests a clean architectural hypothesis about what detection decoders can and cannot extract from shared features, and ships context conditioning as a modular capability if confirmed.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Stuff-thing joint modeling exists in panoptic architectures; explicit stuff-token conditioning of detection queries with a mutual-information-graded prediction appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Add a stuff-token pathway to Deformable DETR (stuff head trained on COCO-Stuff), train matched pairs, compute per-class stuff-context mutual information from annotations, and run the stratified evaluation.
main_risk: Joint training with stuff supervision may improve features globally, requiring a feature-only control (stuff supervision without token conditioning) to isolate the conditioning mechanism.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Detector backbones are assumed to encode all useful context implicitly, making explicit scene structure redundant for modern architectures.
